    77	If the only remaining work is an implementation task, name it briefly and link
    78	the issue or pull request in a footnote.
    79	
    80	\section{When the Investigation Starts}
    81	
    82	The investigation starts when the obstruction appears to be mathematical rather
    83	than merely formal.  No final judgement is needed at this stage.  It is enough
    84	that, after reading the relevant source and attempting the corresponding formal
    85	statement, the proof seems to require a different scalar, an additional
    86	hypothesis, a different tensor placement, a distinction between two objects which
    87	the prose identifies, or an auxiliary assertion not supplied by the cited
    88	argument.
    89	
    90	The same investigation should also start when such a deviation is discovered
    91	after the fact.  If the existing formal development or informal blueprint has
    92	already changed the statement, strengthened a hypothesis, weakened a conclusion,
    93	inserted an unadvertised lemma, or replaced the cited proof by a different
    94	formal-library argument, the mathematical change should be documented even if all
    95	relevant files already compile.
    96	
    97	At this early stage the purpose is to preserve the question while it is still
    98	local.  The note may later conclude that the matter is only notational, that an
    99	intermediate estimate in the cited source needs a harmless correction, that a
   100	missing hypothesis is genuinely needed, or that no discrepancy remains.  Thus
   101	the trigger is not the severity of the eventual verdict, but the appearance of a
   102	real mismatch between the cited reasoning and the statement that can be
   103	formalized.
   104	
   105	A failed tactic search, a missing formal lemma, or an inconvenient coercion is
   106	not enough.  The obstruction must survive translation back into ordinary
   107	mathematics.
   108	
   109	Sometimes an investigation uncovers an improvement that is not a discrepancy:
   110	the formalization works correctly, but it could be simplified by using an
   111	existing library, replacing a custom type, or adopting a cleaner proof route.
   112	These are not, by themselves, paper-gap notes.  They are action items.  When
   113	such an improvement is identified, open a GitHub issue or pull request that
   114	describes the proposed change.  If the investigation also produces a paper-gap
   115	note, link the issue or pull request from that note: the note records the
   116	mathematical justification, and the issue or pull request drives the
   117	implementation.
   118	
   119	\section{When to Write a Note}
   120	
   121	A note should be written once the source argument and the formal proof no longer
   122	match as mathematical arguments.  This includes, for instance, a numerical
   123	estimate whose constant does not follow from the cited lemma, a displayed
   124	conclusion which uses an unstated hypothesis, or a step in which two objects are
   125	identified although they must remain distinct.  In analytic, algebraic,
   126	probabilistic, or quantum arguments, such distinctions may concern the domain of
   127	a map, the placement of a tensor factor, the type of an outcome, the distinction
   128	between a structure and a substructure, or the scalar carried by an approximation
   129	relation.
   130	
   131	A note is required when an audit finds that a Lean declaration associated with a
   132	source-labelled statement has acquired an extra non-source hypothesis, such as
   133	bridge, residual, repair, producer, or obligation-structure data.  Such a
   134	declaration is temporary proof debt, not a replacement for the source theorem,
   135	and should not be introduced merely to avoid a \verb|sorry|.  The note must say
   136	plainly that the Lean result is conditional, identify the source-faithful theorem
   137	form that remains to be proved, and give the intended obligation discharger or
   138	removal plan.  The blueprint should not mark the source-labelled statement with
   139	\verb|\leanok| by pointing to this conditional helper.
   140	
   141	Changing a Lean theorem away from the statement in
   142	\path{references/ldt-paper/} is strongly discouraged.  A paper-gap note should
   143	not make such a change look routine: it should explain the mathematical
   144	necessity, or else classify the change as proof debt to be removed.
   145	
   146	When an existing conditional helper is audited, the first task is to extract any
   147	argument it already contains into source-faithful lemmas.  If the remaining
   148	bridge hypothesis cannot be derived from the paper hypotheses, the formal
   149	development should restore the source theorem statement and record the missing
   150	proof obligation explicitly, rather than retaining the strengthened statement as
   151	though it were the paper theorem.
   152	
   153	This requirement is not meant to classify every explicit Lean side condition as
   154	a discrepancy.  Positivity, nonemptiness, decidability, field-model instances,
   155	and denominator nonvanishing hypotheses may be faithful encodings of the domain
   156	in which the paper's theorem is stated.  The note should distinguish such
   157	boundary hypotheses from hypotheses that supply an unproved step of the paper
   158	argument.
   159	
   160	A note is also appropriate when the proof becomes formal only after changing an
   161	intermediate scalar, weakening a conclusion, strengthening a hypothesis, or
   162	inserting an additional lemma which is not simply an expansion of the cited
   163	argument.  These are mathematical changes, even when they are harmless for the
   164	final theorem.  It is likewise appropriate when an available formal-library
   165	theorem proves the needed result under a somewhat different formulation from the
   166	cited source.  In that case the note should be deliberately pedagogical.  It
   167	should explain, in ordinary mathematical language, what the replacement result
   168	says, how it is specialized, which hypotheses are new or differently packaged,
   169	and why the resulting statement is a legitimate substitute for the step in the
   170	cited argument.  If the issue remains open after reasonable attempts, the note
   171	should say what has been checked and what remains unknown.
   172	
   173	\section{Counterexamples}
   174	
   175	If the cited assertion appears to be false, the note should not stop at saying
   176	that the proof cannot be formalized.  It should give the counterexample, or the
   177	smallest relevant part of it, in ordinary mathematical notation.  The example
   178	should be accompanied by enough verification that the reader can see both sides:
   179	the hypotheses of the cited assertion hold, and its conclusion fails.
   180	
   181	When feasible, the counterexample should also be formalized in \Lean{}.  This is
   182	especially valuable when the example is finite, algebraic, computational, or
   183	otherwise small enough that the failure can be checked without reproducing the
   184	whole surrounding theory.  The note should then state the mathematical content
   185	of the checked counterexample and identify the corresponding Lean declaration in
   186	a footnote.  The Lean file is not a substitute for the prose: the prose should
   187	still explain why the example refutes the cited assertion.
   188	
   189	\section{Revision of a Note}
   190	
   191	A paper-gap note may be provisional.  It may begin as soon as the mathematical
   192	obstruction has been isolated well enough to state the question, and it may be
   193	revised as the calculation, the blueprint, or the corresponding \Lean{}
   194	declarations become clearer.  The first version need not know the final
   195	classification, but it should say plainly which mathematical point is known and
   196	which point remains unsettled.
   197	
   198	Later revisions should not make the note into a chronological log.  They should
   199	rewrite the document so that it remains a coherent account of the present
   200	mathematical understanding.  If the verdict changes, the conclusion should state
   201	the current verdict; the linked issue or pull request can preserve the earlier
   202	discussion.
   203	
   204	\section{Form of the Note}
   205	
   206	Each note should stand on its own.  It should give the date, cite the relevant
   207	source article, and provide enough traceability for the reader to locate the
   208	original passage and the project discussion.  GitHub issues and pull requests may
   209	be linked with \verb|\href|, and source files, line ranges, and labels should be
   210	recorded when they help the reader check the claim.  These references should
   211	serve the exposition rather than govern it: the main text should be organized
   212	around the mathematical assertion and its proof.
   213	
   214	The note should introduce its notation before using it.  Symbols for
   215	measurements, tensor factors, approximation relations, and error parameters
   216	should be named in prose.  If an approximation relation is state-dependent, the
   217	state should be named, or its defining expression should be given when this can
   218	be done briefly.  Only after the notation is in place should the note state the
   219	assertion in the cited source, using a bibliographic citation such as
   220	\verb|\cite[Section~...]{...}| when the section or chapter is known.
   221	
   222	Only the relevant hypotheses should be reproduced.  If the question is a scalar
   223	substitution, a missing term, or a missing hypothesis, the note should not quote
   224	a long unrelated part of the proof.  It should give the cited lemma or
   225	proposition in the special case actually used, then display the calculation or
   226	logical implication in which the discrepancy appears.
   227	
   228	Displayed equations should be used with restraint.  They are appropriate for the
   229	source estimate being checked, the cited estimate in the form actually used, and
   230	the calculation where a term or hypothesis appears or disappears.  When a
   231	displayed equation is identified by a source label, the label should appear on
   232	the right of the display, while the surrounding prose refers to the mathematical
   233	assertion itself.  The standard \texttt{amsmath} command \verb|\tag| is the
   234	right mechanism for this; a separate local convention should be introduced only
   235	if the standard mechanism is genuinely insufficient.  For a multi-line aligned
   236	display, tag the individual lines that carry the source information rather than
   237	forcing a long combined label below the equations.  Short
   238	scalar definitions and elementary inequalities should remain inline when the
   239	sentence reads better that way.  As in ordinary mathematical writing, a displayed
   240	formula is part of the surrounding sentence and should be punctuated accordingly.
   241	
   242	Bibliographic entries used only by these notes should live in
   243	\path{docs/paper-gaps/references.bib}.  A new note should ordinarily begin from
   244	\path{docs/paper-gaps/template.tex}, which records the common LaTeX preamble,
   245	the local bibliography, and a model for right-hand source labels in displayed
   246	equations.
   247	
   248	Blueprint prose cites a note like any other source, with
   249	\verb|\cite{gap:<slug>}|; the bibliography entry in
   250	\path{blueprint/src/references.bib} carries the published URL of the note,
   251	whether the note lives in this repository or in another one.  Lean docstrings
   252	and comments use the repository path form \path{docs/paper-gaps/<slug>.tex}.
   253	
   254	The note should then compare the cited source with the informal blueprint, if
   255	there is one, and with the formal statement.  This comparison should be written
   256	in ordinary mathematical prose.  Formal declaration names and source paths should
   257	be supplied only to identify the exact formal statements, and normally belong in
   258	footnotes.
   259	
   260	The conclusion should give a verdict.  It may say that there is no discrepancy,
   261	that the matter is only notational, that an intermediate estimate needs a
   262	harmless correction, that a hypothesis is missing, that there is a theorem-level
   263	gap, or that the question remains open.  The classification should reflect the
   264	mathematics, not the amount of formal work required.
   265	
   266	\section{Decision Principle}
   267	
   268	The formal development should not silently replace the cited assertion by a
   269	different one.  If the formal statement differs from the cited source, the
   270	reason for the difference should be written down.  Conversely, the note should
   271	not overstate the conclusion.  A wrong intermediate scalar is not a fatal gap in
   272	the theorem if the corrected scalar is bounded by the error parameter appearing
   273	in the theorem statement.
   274	
   275	\end{document}

     4	/-!
     5	# The quantum linearity theorem
     6	
     7	This file states the external quantum-linearity result used to combine the
     8	binary observables produced in the point analysis.  The statement uses a
     9	positive semidefinite trace-one operator, and its conclusion adjoins a finite ancillary
    10	space on which the exactly linear observables act.
    11	
    12	## References
    13	
    14	The declaration is `thm:linearity` in
    15	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:82-180`.  The quotation in the
    16	QPBT paper is at
    17	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:713-725`; the
    18	provider is Theorem 10 of Natarajan--Vidick, arXiv:1610.03574.
    19	-/
    20	
    21	open scoped BigOperators Matrix MatrixOrder ComplexOrder
    22	
    23	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    24	
    25	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    26	open MIPStarRE.Quantum
    27	
    28	noncomputable section
    29	
    30	/-- A binary observable is a Hermitian operator whose square is the identity.
    31	This is the finite-matrix realization of `Obs(H)` in `thm:linearity`, blueprint
    32	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:82-180`, quoted at paper
    33	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:713-725`. -/
    34	def IsBinaryObservable {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    35	    (O : Op ι) : Prop :=
    36	  O.IsHermitian ∧ O * O = 1
    37	
    38	/-- The rank-one density operator associated with an ancillary vector. -/
    39	noncomputable def ancProj {ι : Type} [Fintype ι]
    40	    (v : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) : Op ι :=
    41	  let w := (EuclideanSpace.equiv ι ℂ) v
    42	  Matrix.vecMulVec w (star w)
    43	
    44	/-- Squared state-dependent distance between two operators.  This is the
    45	quantity `d_rho(S,T)^2` in `thm:linearity`, blueprint
    46	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:82-180`. -/
    47	noncomputable def stateDepDistSq {ι : Type} [Fintype ι]
    48	    (S T ρ : Op ι) : ℝ :=
    49	  (Matrix.trace ((S - T)ᴴ * (S - T) * ρ)).re
    50	
    51	/-- The quantum linearity theorem imported from Natarajan--Vidick.
    52	
    53	The statement is `thm:linearity` in
    54	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:82-145`; the QPBT paper quotes
    55	it at
    56	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:713-725`.
    57	
    58	As recorded in `rem:linearity-import` (blueprint lines 147--180), this
    59	provider-faithful form imposes no upper bound on `δ`, preserves the error,
    60	asserts exact linearity for every pair, and averages closeness only over `u`.
    61	The paper quotation instead adds `δ ≤ 1`, phrases closeness pointwise under a
    62	pair quantifier, and appends `L 0 = 1`; those three deviations are not
    63	reproduced.  The identity at zero follows later from exact linearity and the
    64	binary-observable condition. -/
    65	theorem exists_exactly_linear_observables {ι : Type}
    66	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    67	    (t : ℕ) (ht : 0 < t) (δ : ℝ) (hδ : 0 ≤ δ)
    68	    (ρ : Op ι) (hρ : ρ.PosSemidef) (htrace : ρ.trace = 1)
    69	    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι)
    70	    (hO : ∀ u, IsBinaryObservable (O u))
    71	    (hcorrelation :
    72	      1 - δ ≤ avgOver
    73	        (uniformDistribution
    74	          ((Fin t → ZMod 2) × (Fin t → ZMod 2)))
    75	        (fun pair =>
    76	          (Matrix.trace
    77	            (O pair.1 * O pair.2 * O (pair.1 + pair.2) * ρ)).re)) :
    78	    ∃ (ι' : Type) (_ : Fintype ι') (_ : DecidableEq ι')
    79	        (anc : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι'),
    80	      ‖anc‖ = 1 ∧
    81	        ∃ L : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op (ι × ι'),
    82	          (∀ u, IsBinaryObservable (L u)) ∧
    83	          (∀ u u', L u * L u' = L (u + u')) ∧
    84	          avgOver (uniformDistribution (Fin t → ZMod 2))
    85	              (fun u => stateDepDistSq (L u)
    86	                (heteroKron (O u) (1 : Op ι'))
    87	                (heteroKron ρ (ancProj anc))) ≤ δ := by
    88	  sorry
    89	
    90	end
    91	
    92	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

    43	\section{Key theorem forms}
    44	
    45	Let $S$ and $T$ be binary observables and let $\rho$ be a positive
    46	semidefinite operator of trace one.  We distinguish the raw operator distance
    47	from the distance between their associated binary projective measurements:
    48	\begin{align*}
    49	  \draw_\rho(S,T)^2
    50	    &:= \Re\tr\big((S-T)^\dagger(S-T)\rho\big), \\
    51	  \dbin_\rho(S,T)^2
    52	    &:= \sum_{s\in\{+,-\}}
    53	      \Re\tr\big((P_S^s-P_T^s)^\dagger
    54	                       (P_S^s-P_T^s)\rho\big),
    55	  \qquad P_S^\pm := \frac{\Id\pm S}{2}.
    56	\end{align*}
    57	The normalization and correlation identities are
    58	\begin{align}
    59	  \dbin_\rho(S,T)^2 &= \frac12\draw_\rho(S,T)^2,
    60	    \tag{normalization}\label{eq:normalization}\\
    61	  \draw_\rho(S,T)^2
    62	    &= 2-2\Re\tr(ST\rho),
    63	    \tag{raw correlation}\label{eq:raw-correlation}\\
    64	  \dbin_\rho(S,T)^2
    65	    &= 1-\Re\tr(ST\rho).
    66	    \tag{binary correlation}\label{eq:binary-correlation}
    67	\end{align}
    68	Consequently, the conclusion delivered by the quantum linearity argument can
    69	be written either as
    70	\[
    71	  \mathbb E_a\dbin_{\rho'}(\mathcal A(a),A(a))^2\leq\delta
    72	\]
    73	or, equivalently, as
    74	\[
    75	  \mathbb E_a\draw_{\rho'}(\mathcal A(a),A(a))^2\leq2\delta.
    76	\]
    77	These are not equivalent to the same bound $\delta$ for the raw distance.%
    78	\footnote{The formal declarations are \leanid{binaryObservableEffect},

    82	\leanid{binaryObservableDistSq\_eq\_one\_sub\_correlation} in

   127	\section{A four-point counterexample}
   128	
   129	The raw bound with constant $\delta$ is false.  Let
   130	$G=(\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z)^2$, choose $r\in G\setminus\{0\}$, take the
   131	one-dimensional state $\rho=1$, and define scalar binary observables by
   132	\[

   137	\]

   139	coefficients satisfy
   140	\[

   142	  \qquad

   144	\]
   145	Their multiset is

   147	\[
   148	  \mathbb E_{a,b}A(a)A(b)A(a+b)
   149	    =\sum_u\widehat A(u)^3=\frac14.
   150	\]
   151	The correlation hypothesis therefore holds with $\delta=3/4$.

   163	therefore a convex combination of the scalar character correlations above, so

   165	$\delta=3/4$.  By~\eqref{eq:normalization}, the corresponding normalized
   166	distance has lower bound $1/2$, which is compatible with the provider's
   167	conclusion.

   200	
   201	The provider's binary-measurement calculation is correct through the factor

    64	Call a tuple $\omega = (u_\xpt,u_\zpt,r_\xpt,r_\zpt) \in (\F_q^m)^2
    65	\times (\F_q)^2$ \emph{anticommuting} if the quantity 
    66	 \[\gamma\,=\,\tr ((r_\xpt \cdot
    67	\ind_m(u_\xpt)) \cdot (r_\zpt \cdot \ind_m(u_\zpt)))\]
    68	introduced in~\Cref{eq:gamma-value} is not $0$, and \emph{commuting} if $\gamma=0$.
    69	
    70	\begin{fact}
    71	\label{fact:omega-anticomm-prob}
    72		The probability that a tuple $\omega= (u_\xpt,u_\zpt,r_\xpt,r_\zpt)$ sampled uniformly at random from $(\F_q^m)^2 \times (\F_q)^2$
    73		is anti-commuting is at least 
    74		\[
    75			(1 - q^{-m}) \cdot (1 - q^{-1}) \cdot \Big (1 - \frac{md}{q} \Big )  \cdot \frac{1}{2} \geq \Big (1 - \frac{3md}{q} \Big ) \cdot \frac{1}{2}.
    76		\]
    77		The probability that $\omega$ is commuting is also at least $\Big(1 - \frac{3md}{q} \Big ) \cdot \frac{1}{2}$.
    78	\end{fact}
    79	\begin{proof}
    80		First, note that $\ind_m(u_\xpt) = 0$ if and only if $u_\xpt = 0$. If $u_\xpt=0$ then $\omega$ is commuting. Otherwise, if $u_\xpt \neq 0$, then observe that for all $r_\xpt, r_\zpt, u_\zpt$,
    81		\begin{align*}
    82			\tr( (r_\xpt \cdot \ind_m(u_\xpt)) \cdot (r_\zpt \cdot
    83	                \ind_m(u_\zpt))) &= \tr( r_\xpt r_\zpt (\ind_m(u_\xpt) \cdot \ind_m(u_\zpt))) \\
    84									&= \tr( (r_\xpt r_\zpt) \cdot g_{\ind_m(u_\xpt)}(u_\zpt))\;,
    85		\end{align*}
    86		where $g_{\ind_m(u_\xpt)}$ is a nonzero polynomial in $\ideg_{d,m}(\F_q)$.
    87		
    88		If $r_\xpt = 0$, then $\omega$ is commuting. Condition on $r_\xpt \neq 0$.  Since $g_{\ind_m(u_\xpt)}\neq 0$ has total degree at most $md$, by the Schwartz-Zippel lemma the probability that $g_{\ind_m(u_\xpt)}(u_\zpt)$ is zero over a uniformly random choice of $u_\zpt$ is at most $md/q$. Conditioned on $g_{\ind_m(u_\xpt)}(u_\zpt) \neq 0$, the product $(r_\xpt r_\zpt) \cdot g_{\ind_m(u_\xpt)}(u_\zpt)$ is a uniformly random element of $\F_q$ when $r_\zpt$ is chosen uniformly at random. 
    89		
    90		The probability that $u_\xpt \neq 0, r_\xpt \neq 0, g_{\ind_m(u_\xpt)}(u_\zpt) \neq 0$ is at least $(1 - q^{-m}) \cdot (1 - q^{-1}) \cdot (1 - md/q)$ since $u_\xpt, r_\xpt, u_\zpt$ are chosen independently.
    91		
    92		Since $q = 2^t$ is an admissible field size, we have that for all $a \in \F_q$, the trace of $a$ is equal to $\sum_i a_i$ where $(a_1,\ldots,a_t)=\kappa(a) \in \F_2^t$ are defined in Section~\ref{sec:subfields}. Thus the probability that a uniformly random element of $\F_q$ has trace $0$ is exactly $1/2$. 
    93	\end{proof}
    94	
    95	In this appendix we often use the ``$\approx_\delta$'' notation to specify closeness of general operators (not necessarily POVMs) that are indexed by questions but not answers: given sets of operators $\{A^x \}$ and $\{B^x\}$ indexed by questions $x \in \cal{X}$, we write $A^x \approx_\delta B^x$ to denote \[
    96		\E_{x \sim \mu} \bra{\psi} (A^x - B^x)^\dagger (A^x - B^x)
    97	        \ket{\psi}\,\leq\, O(\delta)
    98	      \]
    99	where $\mu$ is a question distribution and $\ket{\psi}$ is a state that has been fixed by context. This will be useful for expressing closeness of observables, for example. The following two lemmas relate the closeness between sets of operators and weighted sums of those operators. 
   100	\begin{lemma}
   101	\label{lem:avg-closeness}
   102	Let $\{A^x \}$ and $\{B^x\}$ be operators indexed by some finite set $\mathcal{X}$, and let $\mu$ be a probability distribution over $\mathcal{X}$. Let $\{\alpha_x \}$ be a set of complex numbers such that $|\alpha_x| \leq 1$. Then if $A^x \approx_\delta B^x$ on average over $x$ drawn from $\mu$, then $A \approx_\delta B$, where $A = \E_x \alpha_x A^x$ and $B= \E_x \alpha_x B^x$.
   103	\end{lemma}
   104	\begin{proof}
   105	Expand
   106	\begin{align*}
   107		\Big\| \E_x \alpha_x \big ( A^x - B^x \big) \ket{\psi} \Big\|^2 &\leq \Big( \E_x \norm{ (A^x -B^x) \ket{\psi}} \Big)^2 \\
   108		&\leq \E_x \norm{(A^x - B^x) \ket{\psi}}^2 \\
   109		&\leq \delta\;.
   110	\end{align*}
   111	The first inequality is the triangle inequality and the second inequality is Jensen's inequality. 
   112	\end{proof}
   113	
   114	\begin{lemma}
   115	\label{lem:povm-to-obs}
   116	Let $\mathcal{A}$ be a finite set. Let $\{A^x_a \}_{a \in \mathcal{A}}$ and $\{B^x_a\}_{a \in \mathcal{A}}$ be POVMs and let $\{ \alpha_a \}_{a \in \mathcal{A}}$ be a collection of complex numbers on the unit circle. Let $A^x = \sum_a \alpha_a A^x_a$ and $B^x = \sum_a  \alpha_a B^x_a$. Then 
   117	\[
   118		A^x_a \approx_\delta B^x_a \quad \text{implies} \quad A^x \approx_{\delta'} B^x
   119	\]
   120	for $\delta' = |\mathcal{A}| \cdot \delta$.
   121	\end{lemma}
   122	\begin{proof}
   123	Expand
   124		\begin{align*}
   125			\E_x \norm{(A^x - B^x) \ket{\psi}}^2 &= \E_x \Big\|\sum_a \alpha_a (A^x_a - B^x_a) \ket{\psi}\Big\|^2 \\
   126			&\leq \E_x \Big( \sum_a \norm{ (A^x_a - B^x_a) \ket{\psi}} \Big)^2 \\
   127			&\leq \E_x |\mathcal{A}| \cdot \sum_a \norm{ (A^x_a - B^x_a) \ket{\psi}}^2 \\
   128			&\leq |\mathcal{A}| \cdot \delta\;.
   129		\end{align*}
   130	The first inequality follows from the triangle inequality, the second inequality follows from Cauchy-Schwarz, and the last inequality follows from the assumption that $A^x_a \approx_\delta B^x_a$. 
   131	\end{proof}

   134	The following lemma shows that POVMs that are approximately projective (in the sense of being self-consistent) are close to exact projective measurements. The lemma first appears in~\cite{KV11}; for a self-contained proof, see~\cite{ML20}.
   135	
   136	\begin{lemma}[Orthonormalization lemma]\label{lem:ortho}
   137	Let $0\leq \delta\leq 1$. There exists a function $\eta_{ortho}(\delta)\,=\, O\big(\delta^{1/4}\big)$ such that the following holds.  Let $\ket{\psi}$ be a state on $\mH_\alice \otimes \mH_\bob$ where $\mH_\alice,\mH_\bob$ are finite dimensional. Let $\{Q_a\}$ and $\{R_a\}$ be POVM on $\mH_\alice$ and $\mH_\bob$ respectively such that 
   138	\begin{equation}\label{eq:cons-cond} 
   139	Q_a \abc R_a \,.
   140	\end{equation}
   141	Then there exists a projective measurement $\{P_a\}$ such that
   142	\begin{equation}\label{eq:cons-ccl}
   143	  P_a \otimes \Id_\bob \,\approx_{\eta_{ortho}} Q_a \otimes \Id_\bob \;.
   144	\end{equation}
   145	\end{lemma}

     4	/-!
     5	# The operator-valued BLR bound
     6	
     7	This file carries out the Fourier-analytic part of the proof of the quantum
     8	linearity theorem of Natarajan and Vidick.  Given binary observables `O^u`
     9	indexed by the Boolean cube `(ZMod 2)^t` and a positive semidefinite trace-one
    10	operator `ρ`, it expresses the state-dependent multiplicative defect of the
    11	family through the two-query correlation of the linearity test, identifies the
    12	sum of the cubic Fourier coefficients with that correlation, and records the
    13	overlap certificate for the Fourier-square POVM `B^u = (hat O^u)^2` that the
    14	Naimark dilation consumes.  Pairwise commutation of the observables is never
    15	assumed, and every complex trace is handled through its real part.
    16	
    17	## Main results
    18	
    19	* `multiplicativeDefect`: the state-dependent squared defect of `O^u O^v`
    20	  from `O^{u+v}`.
    21	* `avg_multiplicativeDefect_eq_two_sub_two_mul_correlation` and
    22	  `avg_multiplicativeDefect_le_two_mul_error`: the average defect equals
    23	  `2 - 2 * (correlation)`, hence is at most `2 * δ` under the correlation
    24	  hypothesis of `exists_exactly_linear_observables`.
    25	* `operatorFourier_cube_trace_eq_correlation`: the identity
    26	  `∑_u Tr_ρ((hat O^u)^3) = E_{a,b} Tr_ρ(O^a O^b O^{a+b})`.
    27	* `fourierSquareMeasurement` and `one_sub_error_le_avg_overlap_fourierSquare`:
    28	  the Fourier-square POVM together with its overlap certificate.
    29	
    30	## References
    31	
    32	Natarajan--Vidick, arXiv:1610.03574, Theorem 10 with displays (7)--(8) and
    33	its proof, `references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1074-1113`; the state-dependent
    34	distance is defined at lines 866--900 of the same file.  The QPBT paper quotes
    35	the theorem at
    36	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:711-725` and
    37	invokes it at lines 787--832.  The blueprint statement is `thm:linearity` in
    38	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:81-147`.  The normalization of
    39	the error constant is analyzed in
    40	`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_linearity-distance-normalization.tex`: the exact defect
    41	bound is `2 * δ` for the raw distance `stateDepDistSq`, equivalently `δ` for
    42	the normalized binary-observable distance.
    43	-/
    44	
    45	open scoped BigOperators Matrix MatrixOrder ComplexOrder
    46

    54	/-! ## The two-query correlation and the multiplicative defect -/
    55	
    56	/-- The two-query correlation of the linearity test: the average, over a
    57	uniformly random pair `(u, u')` in `(ZMod 2)^t`, of the real part of
    58	`Tr(O^u O^{u'} O^{u+u'} ρ)`.  This is the left-hand side of display (7) in
    59	Natarajan--Vidick, `references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1078-1080`, and the
    60	quantity bounded below in the hypothesis of
    61	`exists_exactly_linear_observables`; the order of the two uniform variables is
    62	the one used there. -/
    63	def blrCorrelation {t : ℕ} {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    64	    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (ρ : Op ι) : ℝ :=
    65	  avgOver (uniformDistribution ((Fin t → ZMod 2) × (Fin t → ZMod 2)))
    66	    (fun pair =>
    67	      (Matrix.trace (O pair.1 * O pair.2 * O (pair.1 + pair.2) * ρ)).re)
    68	
    69	/-- The state-dependent squared defect of the product `O^u O^v` from `O^{u+v}`,
    70	namely `d_ρ(O^u O^v, O^{u+v})^2` for the state-dependent distance of
    71	`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:873-875`.  Its average over uniformly random
    72	`u, v` is the approximate-linearity error of the family in the sense of the QPBT
    73	quotation `references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:713-718`,
    74	measured with the raw distance `stateDepDistSq`. -/
    75	def multiplicativeDefect {t : ℕ} {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    76	    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (ρ : Op ι) (u v : Fin t → ZMod 2) : ℝ :=
    77	  stateDepDistSq (O u * O v) (O (u + v)) ρ
    78	
    79	/-- Pointwise form of the defect identity: for binary observables the squared
    80	defect of `O^u O^v` from `O^{u+v}` is `2 - 2 Re Tr(O^v O^u O^{v+u} ρ)`.  The
    81	expansion of `(O^u O^v - O^{u+v})^† (O^u O^v - O^{u+v})` produces the two
    82	triple products `O^v O^u O^{u+v}` and `O^{u+v} O^u O^v`; the second is the
    83	adjoint of the first, so their traces against `ρ` are complex conjugates with
    84	equal real parts.  This is the calculation behind display (3) of
    85	`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:900-912`, applied to the products of the
    86	family. -/
    87	theorem multiplicativeDefect_eq_two_sub_two_mul_correlation {t : ℕ}
    88	    {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    89	    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (hO : ∀ a, IsBinaryObservable (O a))
    90	    (ρ : Op ι) (hρ : ρ.PosSemidef) (htrace : ρ.trace = 1)
    91	    (u v : Fin t → ZMod 2) :
    92	    multiplicativeDefect O ρ u v =
    93	      2 - 2 * (Matrix.trace (O v * O u * O (v + u) * ρ)).re := by
    94	  have hu := hO u
    95	  have hv := hO v
    96	  have huv := hO (u + v)
    97	  have hdiff :
    98	      (O u * O v - O (u + v))ᴴ * (O u * O v - O (u + v)) =
    99	        (2 : ℂ) • (1 : Op ι) - O v * O u * O (u + v) - O (u + v) * O u * O v := by
   100	    rw [Matrix.conjTranspose_sub, Matrix.conjTranspose_mul, hu.1.eq, hv.1.eq,
   101	      huv.1.eq]
   102	    calc
   103	      (O v * O u - O (u + v)) * (O u * O v - O (u + v)) =
   104	          O v * (O u * O u) * O v - O v * O u * O (u + v) -
   105	            O (u + v) * O u * O v + O (u + v) * O (u + v) := by
   106	        noncomm_ring
   107	      _ = (2 : ℂ) • (1 : Op ι) - O v * O u * O (u + v) -
   108	            O (u + v) * O u * O v := by
   109	        rw [hu.2, Matrix.mul_one, hv.2, huv.2]
   110	        module
   111	  have hstar :
   112	      star (Matrix.trace (O (u + v) * O u * O v * ρ)) =
   113	        Matrix.trace (O v * O u * O (u + v) * ρ) := by
   114	    calc
   115	      star (Matrix.trace (O (u + v) * O u * O v * ρ)) =
   116	          Matrix.trace ((O (u + v) * O u * O v * ρ)ᴴ) := by
   117	        rw [Matrix.trace_conjTranspose]
   118	      _ = Matrix.trace (ρ * (O v * O u * O (u + v))) := by
   119	        simp [Matrix.conjTranspose_mul, hu.1.eq, hv.1.eq, huv.1.eq,
   120	          hρ.isHermitian.eq, Matrix.mul_assoc]
   121	      _ = Matrix.trace (O v * O u * O (u + v) * ρ) := by
   122	        exact Matrix.trace_mul_comm _ _
   123	  have hcross :
   124	      (Matrix.trace (O (u + v) * O u * O v * ρ)).re =
   125	        (Matrix.trace (O v * O u * O (u + v) * ρ)).re := by
   126	    have := congrArg Complex.re hstar
   127	    simpa [Complex.star_def, Complex.conj_re] using this
   128	  unfold multiplicativeDefect stateDepDistSq
   129	  rw [hdiff]
   130	  simp only [Matrix.sub_mul, Matrix.trace_sub, Complex.sub_re]
   131	  rw [smul_mul_assoc, one_mul, Matrix.trace_smul, htrace]
   132	  norm_num [Complex.mul_re]
   133	  rw [hcross, add_comm v u]
   134	  ring
   135	
   136	/-- The average multiplicative defect over a uniformly random pair equals
   137	`2 - 2 * (two-query correlation)`.  The pointwise identity
   138	`multiplicativeDefect_eq_two_sub_two_mul_correlation` produces the correlation
   139	summand with the two variables in reversed order; since the pair is uniform,
   140	exchanging the two coordinates leaves the average unchanged.  This is the
   141	relation between the approximate-linearity hypothesis of the QPBT quotation
   142	(`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:713-718`) and
   143	display (7) of Natarajan--Vidick (`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1078-1080`),
   144	in the raw normalization of
   145	`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_linearity-distance-normalization.tex`. -/
   146	theorem avg_multiplicativeDefect_eq_two_sub_two_mul_correlation {t : ℕ}
   147	    {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   148	    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (hO : ∀ a, IsBinaryObservable (O a))
   149	    (ρ : Op ι) (hρ : ρ.PosSemidef) (htrace : ρ.trace = 1) :
   150	    avgOver (uniformDistribution ((Fin t → ZMod 2) × (Fin t → ZMod 2)))
   151	        (fun pair => multiplicativeDefect O ρ pair.1 pair.2) =
   152	      2 - 2 * blrCorrelation O ρ := by
   153	  have hswap :
   154	      avgOver (uniformDistribution ((Fin t → ZMod 2) × (Fin t → ZMod 2)))
   155	        (fun pair =>
   156	          (Matrix.trace (O pair.2 * O pair.1 * O (pair.2 + pair.1) * ρ)).re) =
   157	        blrCorrelation O ρ := by
   158	    unfold blrCorrelation
   159	    refine (avgOver_uniform_equiv (Equiv.prodComm _ _) _).trans ?_
   160	    exact avgOver_congr _ _ _ (fun pair => rfl)
   161	  calc
   162	    avgOver (uniformDistribution ((Fin t → ZMod 2) × (Fin t → ZMod 2)))
   163	        (fun pair => multiplicativeDefect O ρ pair.1 pair.2) =
   164	        avgOver (uniformDistribution ((Fin t → ZMod 2) × (Fin t → ZMod 2)))
   165	          (fun pair => 2 - 2 *
   166	            (Matrix.trace (O pair.2 * O pair.1 * O (pair.2 + pair.1) * ρ)).re) :=
   167	      avgOver_congr _ _ _ (fun pair =>
   168	        multiplicativeDefect_eq_two_sub_two_mul_correlation O hO ρ hρ htrace
   169	          pair.1 pair.2)
   170	    _ = 2 - 2 * blrCorrelation O ρ := by
   171	      rw [avgOver_sub, avgOver_const_mul, avgOver_uniform_const, hswap]
   172	
   173	/-- The operator-valued BLR bound: under the correlation hypothesis of
   174	`exists_exactly_linear_observables`, the average squared defect of `O^u O^v`
   175	from `O^{u+v}` is at most `2 * δ`.  This is the passage from display (7) of
   176	Natarajan--Vidick (`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1078-1080`) to the
   177	approximate-linearity relation of the QPBT quotation
   178	(`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:713-718`); the
   179	constant `2` is the raw-distance normalization recorded in
   180	`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_linearity-distance-normalization.tex`. -/
   181	theorem avg_multiplicativeDefect_le_two_mul_error {t : ℕ}
   182	    {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   183	    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (hO : ∀ a, IsBinaryObservable (O a))
   184	    (ρ : Op ι) (hρ : ρ.PosSemidef) (htrace : ρ.trace = 1)
   185	    (δ : ℝ) (hcorrelation : 1 - δ ≤ blrCorrelation O ρ) :
   186	    avgOver (uniformDistribution ((Fin t → ZMod 2) × (Fin t → ZMod 2)))
   187	        (fun pair => multiplicativeDefect O ρ pair.1 pair.2) ≤ 2 * δ := by
   188	  rw [avg_multiplicativeDefect_eq_two_sub_two_mul_correlation O hO ρ hρ htrace]
   189	  linarith
   190	
   191	/-! ## The cubic Fourier identity -/
   192	
   193	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma for the Fourier computations in the
   194	proof of Theorem 10 of Natarajan--Vidick
   195	(`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1096-1112`): a twisted form of the
   196	matrix-valued Parseval identity in which only the first factor is expanded
   197	through its Fourier coefficients.  Taking `a = 0` recovers Parseval. -/
   198	private theorem sum_booleanCharacter_smul_operatorFourier_mul {t : ℕ}
   199	    {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   200	    (A X : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (a : Fin t → ZMod 2) :
   201	    ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2,
   202	        booleanCharacter u a • (operatorFourier A u * X u) =
   203	      ((Fintype.card (Fin t → ZMod 2) : ℂ)⁻¹) •
   204	        ∑ b : Fin t → ZMod 2,
   205	          A b * ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2, booleanCharacter u (a + b) • X u := by
   206	  classical
   207	  let N : ℂ := Fintype.card (Fin t → ZMod 2)
   208	  calc
   209	    ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2,
   210	        booleanCharacter u a • (operatorFourier A u * X u) =
   211	        ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2, N⁻¹ • ∑ b : Fin t → ZMod 2,
   212	          booleanCharacter u (a + b) • (A b * X u) := by
   213	      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   214	      intro u _
   215	      simp only [operatorFourier, N, smul_mul_assoc, Finset.sum_mul,
   216	        Finset.smul_sum, smul_smul, booleanCharacter_add_right]
   217	      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   218	      intro b _
   219	      congr 1
   220	      ring
   221	    _ = N⁻¹ • ∑ b : Fin t → ZMod 2, ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2,
   222	          booleanCharacter u (a + b) • (A b * X u) := by
   223	      rw [← Finset.smul_sum]
   224	      congr 1
   225	      exact Finset.sum_comm
   226	    _ = N⁻¹ • ∑ b : Fin t → ZMod 2,
   227	          A b * ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2, booleanCharacter u (a + b) • X u := by
   228	      congr 1
   229	      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   230	      intro b _
   231	      rw [Finset.mul_sum]
   232	      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   233	      intro u _
   234	      rw [mul_smul_comm]
   235	
   236	/-- The sum of the cubes of the Fourier coefficients of an operator family is
   237	the average of `O^a O^b O^{a+b}` over a uniformly random pair `(a, b)`.  This
   238	is the operator form of the identity
   239	`∑_u (hat A^u)^3 = E_{a,b} A(a) A(b) A(a+b)` invoked at
   240	`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1111-1112`; the order of the three factors
   241	is preserved throughout. -/
   242	theorem sum_operatorFourier_cube {t : ℕ} {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   243	    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) :
   244	    ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2,
   245	        operatorFourier O u * operatorFourier O u * operatorFourier O u =
   246	      ((Fintype.card ((Fin t → ZMod 2) × (Fin t → ZMod 2)) : ℂ)⁻¹) •
   247	        ∑ p : (Fin t → ZMod 2) × (Fin t → ZMod 2),
   248	          O p.1 * O p.2 * O (p.1 + p.2) := by
   249	  classical
   250	  let N : ℂ := Fintype.card (Fin t → ZMod 2)
   251	  have hinner : ∀ b : Fin t → ZMod 2,
   252	      ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2,
   253	          booleanCharacter u b • (operatorFourier O u * operatorFourier O u) =
   254	        N⁻¹ • ∑ c : Fin t → ZMod 2, O c * O (b + c) := by
   255	    intro b
   256	    rw [sum_booleanCharacter_smul_operatorFourier_mul]

   231	families is preserved. -/
   232	theorem sum_operatorFourier_mul_operatorFourier {t : ℕ} {ι : Type*}
   233	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   234	    (A B : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) :
   235	    ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2, operatorFourier A u * operatorFourier B u =
   236	      ((Fintype.card (Fin t → ZMod 2) : ℂ)⁻¹) •
   237	        ∑ a : Fin t → ZMod 2, A a * B a := by
   238	  classical
   239	  let N : ℂ := Fintype.card (Fin t → ZMod 2)
   240	  calc
   241	    ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2, operatorFourier A u * operatorFourier B u =
   242	        ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2, N⁻¹ •
   243	          ∑ a : Fin t → ZMod 2,
   244	            (booleanCharacter u a • A a) * operatorFourier B u := by
   245	      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   246	      intro u _
   247	      change (N⁻¹ • ∑ a : Fin t → ZMod 2, booleanCharacter u a • A a) *
   248	          operatorFourier B u = _
   249	      rw [smul_mul_assoc, Finset.sum_mul]
   250	    _ = N⁻¹ • ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2, ∑ a : Fin t → ZMod 2,
   251	          (booleanCharacter u a • A a) * operatorFourier B u := by
   252	      rw [Finset.smul_sum]
   253	    _ = N⁻¹ • ∑ a : Fin t → ZMod 2, ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2,
   254	          (booleanCharacter u a • A a) * operatorFourier B u := by
   255	      congr 1
   256	      rw [Finset.sum_comm]
   257	    _ = N⁻¹ • ∑ a : Fin t → ZMod 2,
   258	          A a * (∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2,
   259	            booleanCharacter u a • operatorFourier B u) := by
   260	      congr 1
   261	      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   262	      intro a _
   263	      rw [Finset.mul_sum]
   264	      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   265	      intro u _
   266	      rw [smul_mul_assoc, mul_smul_comm]
   267	    _ = N⁻¹ • ∑ a : Fin t → ZMod 2, A a * B a := by
   268	      congr 1
   269	      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   270	      intro a _
   271	      rw [operatorFourier_inversion]
   272	    _ = ((Fintype.card (Fin t → ZMod 2) : ℂ)⁻¹) •
   273	          ∑ a : Fin t → ZMod 2, A a * B a := by
   274	      rfl

   277	`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1095-1100`: Parseval specialized to the
   278	square of a single operator family. -/
   279	theorem sum_operatorFourier_sq {t : ℕ} {ι : Type*}
   280	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   281	    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) :
   282	    ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2, operatorFourier O u * operatorFourier O u =
   283	      ((Fintype.card (Fin t → ZMod 2) : ℂ)⁻¹) •
   284	        ∑ a : Fin t → ZMod 2, O a * O a :=
   285	  sum_operatorFourier_mul_operatorFourier O O

   288	coefficients sum to the identity.  This is the Parseval step asserting that
   289	`B^u = (hat A^u)^2` is a POVM in
   290	`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1096-1100`. -/

   292	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   293	    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι)
   294	    (hO : ∀ a, IsBinaryObservable (O a)) :
   295	    ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2, operatorFourier O u * operatorFourier O u = 1 := by
   296	  rw [sum_operatorFourier_sq]

   300	  rw [smul_smul]
   301	  simp

   303	/-! ## Observable-distance normalization -/
   304	
   305	/-- The effect of a binary projective measurement obtained from an observable.
   306	The two effects are `(1 + O) / 2` and `(1 - O) / 2`. -/
   307	noncomputable def binaryObservableEffect {ι : Type} [Fintype ι]
   308	    [DecidableEq ι] (outcome : Bool) (O : Op ι) : Op ι :=
   309	  if outcome then ((2 : ℂ)⁻¹) • (1 - O) else ((2 : ℂ)⁻¹) • (1 + O)
   310	
   311	/-- The squared distance between the binary projective measurements associated
   312	with two observables, summed over their two effects.  This is the measurement
   313	distance calculated in `references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:900-912`; its relation
   314	to `stateDepDistSq` is recorded in
   315	`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_linearity-distance-normalization.tex`. -/
   316	noncomputable def binaryObservableDistSq {ι : Type} [Fintype ι]
   317	    [DecidableEq ι] (S T ρ : Op ι) : ℝ :=
   318	  ∑ outcome : Bool,
   319	    stateDepDistSq (binaryObservableEffect outcome S)
   320	      (binaryObservableEffect outcome T) ρ
   321	
   322	/-- The binary-measurement distance is half the state-dependent operator
   323	distance.
   324	
   325	**Local fix:** Source equation (3) at
   326	`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:903-911` ends by identifying the
   327	binary-measurement distance with the state-dependent operator distance of the
   328	two observables; the correct relation carries the factor `1 / 2` proved here.
   329	Documented in
   330	`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_linearity-distance-normalization.tex`. -/
   331	theorem binaryObservableDistSq_eq_stateDepDistSq_div_two
   332	    {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (S T ρ : Op ι) :
   333	    binaryObservableDistSq S T ρ = stateDepDistSq S T ρ / 2 := by
   334	  simp only [binaryObservableDistSq, Fintype.univ_bool, stateDepDistSq,
   335	    binaryObservableEffect, smul_add, Matrix.conjTranspose_sub,
   336	    Finset.mem_singleton, Bool.true_eq_false, not_false_eq_true,
   337	    Finset.sum_insert, reduceIte, Matrix.conjTranspose_smul, star_inv₀,
   338	    star_ofNat, Matrix.conjTranspose_one, Finset.sum_singleton,
   339	    Bool.false_eq_true, Matrix.conjTranspose_add, add_sub_add_left_eq_sub]
   340	  have hminusStar :
   341	      (2 : ℂ)⁻¹ • (1 - Sᴴ) - (2 : ℂ)⁻¹ • (1 - Tᴴ) =
   342	        -((2 : ℂ)⁻¹ • (Sᴴ - Tᴴ)) := by
   343	    module
   344	  have hminus :
   345	      (2 : ℂ)⁻¹ • (1 - S) - (2 : ℂ)⁻¹ • (1 - T) =
   346	        -((2 : ℂ)⁻¹ • (S - T)) := by
   347	    module
   348	  have hplusStar :
   349	      (2 : ℂ)⁻¹ • Sᴴ - (2 : ℂ)⁻¹ • Tᴴ =
   350	        (2 : ℂ)⁻¹ • (Sᴴ - Tᴴ) := by
   351	    module
   352	  have hplus :
   353	      (2 : ℂ)⁻¹ • S - (2 : ℂ)⁻¹ • T =
   354	        (2 : ℂ)⁻¹ • (S - T) := by
   355	    module
   356	  rw [hminusStar, hminus, hplusStar, hplus]
   357	  simp only [neg_mul, mul_neg, neg_neg, smul_mul_assoc, Matrix.trace_smul]
   358	  norm_num [Complex.mul_re]
   359	  ring
   360	
   361	/-- The state-dependent squared distance between binary observables in terms
   362	of their correlation. -/
   363	theorem stateDepDistSq_eq_two_sub_two_mul_correlation
   364	    {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   365	    (S T ρ : Op ι) (hS : IsBinaryObservable S)
   366	    (hT : IsBinaryObservable T) (hρ : ρ.PosSemidef)
   367	    (htrace : Matrix.trace ρ = 1) :
   368	    stateDepDistSq S T ρ =
   369	      2 - 2 * (Matrix.trace (S * T * ρ)).re := by
   370	  have hstar :
   371	      star (Matrix.trace (S * T * ρ)) = Matrix.trace (T * S * ρ) := by
   372	    calc
   373	      star (Matrix.trace (S * T * ρ)) = Matrix.trace ((S * T * ρ)ᴴ) := by
   374	        rw [Matrix.trace_conjTranspose]
   375	      _ = Matrix.trace (ρ * T * S) := by
   376	        simp [Matrix.conjTranspose_mul, hS.1.eq, hT.1.eq, hρ.isHermitian.eq,
   377	          Matrix.mul_assoc]
   378	      _ = Matrix.trace (T * S * ρ) := by
   379	        exact (Matrix.trace_mul_cycle T S ρ).symm
   380	  have hcross :
   381	      (Matrix.trace (S * T * ρ)).re = (Matrix.trace (T * S * ρ)).re := by
   382	    have := congrArg Complex.re hstar
   383	    simpa [Complex.star_def, Complex.conj_re] using this
   384	  have hdiff :
   385	      (S - T)ᴴ * (S - T) =
   386	        (2 : ℂ) • (1 : Op ι) - S * T - T * S := by
   387	    rw [Matrix.conjTranspose_sub, hS.1.eq, hT.1.eq]
   388	    calc
   389	      (S - T) * (S - T) = S * S - S * T - T * S + T * T := by
   390	        noncomm_ring
   391	      _ = (2 : ℂ) • (1 : Op ι) - S * T - T * S := by
   392	        rw [hS.2, hT.2]
   393	        module
   394	  unfold stateDepDistSq
   395	  rw [hdiff]
   396	  simp only [Matrix.sub_mul, Matrix.trace_sub, Complex.sub_re]
   397	  rw [smul_mul_assoc, one_mul, Matrix.trace_smul, htrace]
   398	  norm_num [Complex.mul_re]
   399	  rw [hcross]
   400	  ring
   401	
   402	/-- The binary-measurement distance is one minus the real state-dependent
   403	correlation. -/
   404	theorem binaryObservableDistSq_eq_one_sub_correlation
   405	    {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   406	    (S T ρ : Op ι) (hS : IsBinaryObservable S)
   407	    (hT : IsBinaryObservable T) (hρ : ρ.PosSemidef)
   408	    (htrace : Matrix.trace ρ = 1) :
   409	    binaryObservableDistSq S T ρ =
   410	      1 - (Matrix.trace (S * T * ρ)).re := by
   411	  rw [binaryObservableDistSq_eq_stateDepDistSq_div_two,
   412	    stateDepDistSq_eq_two_sub_two_mul_correlation S T ρ hS hT hρ htrace]
   413	  ring

   232	theorem sum_operatorFourier_mul_operatorFourier {t : ℕ} {ι : Type*}
   233	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   234	    (A B : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) :
   235	    ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2, operatorFourier A u * operatorFourier B u =
   236	      ((Fintype.card (Fin t → ZMod 2) : ℂ)⁻¹) •
   237	        ∑ a : Fin t → ZMod 2, A a * B a := by
   238	  classical
   239	  let N : ℂ := Fintype.card (Fin t → ZMod 2)
   240	  calc
   241	    ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2, operatorFourier A u * operatorFourier B u =
   242	        ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2, N⁻¹ •
   243	          ∑ a : Fin t → ZMod 2,
   244	            (booleanCharacter u a • A a) * operatorFourier B u := by
   245	      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   246	      intro u _
   247	      change (N⁻¹ • ∑ a : Fin t → ZMod 2, booleanCharacter u a • A a) *
   248	          operatorFourier B u = _
   249	      rw [smul_mul_assoc, Finset.sum_mul]
   250	    _ = N⁻¹ • ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2, ∑ a : Fin t → ZMod 2,
   251	          (booleanCharacter u a • A a) * operatorFourier B u := by
   252	      rw [Finset.smul_sum]
   253	    _ = N⁻¹ • ∑ a : Fin t → ZMod 2, ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2,
   254	          (booleanCharacter u a • A a) * operatorFourier B u := by
   255	      congr 1
   256	      rw [Finset.sum_comm]
   257	    _ = N⁻¹ • ∑ a : Fin t → ZMod 2,
   258	          A a * (∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2,
   259	            booleanCharacter u a • operatorFourier B u) := by
   260	      congr 1
   261	      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   262	      intro a _
   263	      rw [Finset.mul_sum]
   264	      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   265	      intro u _
   266	      rw [smul_mul_assoc, mul_smul_comm]
   267	    _ = N⁻¹ • ∑ a : Fin t → ZMod 2, A a * B a := by
   268	      congr 1
   269	      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   270	      intro a _
   271	      rw [operatorFourier_inversion]

   303	/-! ## Observable-distance normalization -/
   304	
   305	/-- The effect of a binary projective measurement obtained from an observable.
   306	The two effects are `(1 + O) / 2` and `(1 - O) / 2`. -/
   307	noncomputable def binaryObservableEffect {ι : Type} [Fintype ι]
   308	    [DecidableEq ι] (outcome : Bool) (O : Op ι) : Op ι :=
   309	  if outcome then ((2 : ℂ)⁻¹) • (1 - O) else ((2 : ℂ)⁻¹) • (1 + O)
   310	
   311	/-- The squared distance between the binary projective measurements associated
   312	with two observables, summed over their two effects.  This is the measurement
   313	distance calculated in `references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:900-912`; its relation
   314	to `stateDepDistSq` is recorded in
   315	`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_linearity-distance-normalization.tex`. -/
   316	noncomputable def binaryObservableDistSq {ι : Type} [Fintype ι]
   317	    [DecidableEq ι] (S T ρ : Op ι) : ℝ :=
   318	  ∑ outcome : Bool,
   319	    stateDepDistSq (binaryObservableEffect outcome S)
   320	      (binaryObservableEffect outcome T) ρ
   321	
   322	/-- The binary-measurement distance is half the state-dependent operator
   323	distance.
   324	
   325	**Local fix:** Source equation (3) at
   326	`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:903-911` ends by identifying the
   327	binary-measurement distance with the state-dependent operator distance of the
   328	two observables; the correct relation carries the factor `1 / 2` proved here.
   329	Documented in
   330	`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_linearity-distance-normalization.tex`. -/
   331	theorem binaryObservableDistSq_eq_stateDepDistSq_div_two
   332	    {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (S T ρ : Op ι) :
   333	    binaryObservableDistSq S T ρ = stateDepDistSq S T ρ / 2 := by
   334	  simp only [binaryObservableDistSq, Fintype.univ_bool, stateDepDistSq,
   335	    binaryObservableEffect, smul_add, Matrix.conjTranspose_sub,
   336	    Finset.mem_singleton, Bool.true_eq_false, not_false_eq_true,
   337	    Finset.sum_insert, reduceIte, Matrix.conjTranspose_smul, star_inv₀,
   338	    star_ofNat, Matrix.conjTranspose_one, Finset.sum_singleton,
   339	    Bool.false_eq_true, Matrix.conjTranspose_add, add_sub_add_left_eq_sub]
   340	  have hminusStar :
   341	      (2 : ℂ)⁻¹ • (1 - Sᴴ) - (2 : ℂ)⁻¹ • (1 - Tᴴ) =
   342	        -((2 : ℂ)⁻¹ • (Sᴴ - Tᴴ)) := by

   351	    module
   352	  have hplus :

   361	/-- The state-dependent squared distance between binary observables in terms
   362	of their correlation. -/
   363	theorem stateDepDistSq_eq_two_sub_two_mul_correlation
   364	    {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   365	    (S T ρ : Op ι) (hS : IsBinaryObservable S)
   366	    (hT : IsBinaryObservable T) (hρ : ρ.PosSemidef)
   367	    (htrace : Matrix.trace ρ = 1) :
   368	    stateDepDistSq S T ρ =
   369	      2 - 2 * (Matrix.trace (S * T * ρ)).re := by
   370	  have hstar :
   371	      star (Matrix.trace (S * T * ρ)) = Matrix.trace (T * S * ρ) := by
   372	    calc
   373	      star (Matrix.trace (S * T * ρ)) = Matrix.trace ((S * T * ρ)ᴴ) := by
   374	        rw [Matrix.trace_conjTranspose]
   375	      _ = Matrix.trace (ρ * T * S) := by
   376	        simp [Matrix.conjTranspose_mul, hS.1.eq, hT.1.eq, hρ.isHermitian.eq,
   377	          Matrix.mul_assoc]
   378	      _ = Matrix.trace (T * S * ρ) := by
   379	        exact (Matrix.trace_mul_cycle T S ρ).symm
   380	  have hcross :
   381	      (Matrix.trace (S * T * ρ)).re = (Matrix.trace (T * S * ρ)).re := by
   382	    have := congrArg Complex.re hstar
   383	    simpa [Complex.star_def, Complex.conj_re] using this
   384	  have hdiff :
   385	      (S - T)ᴴ * (S - T) =
   386	        (2 : ℂ) • (1 : Op ι) - S * T - T * S := by
   387	    rw [Matrix.conjTranspose_sub, hS.1.eq, hT.1.eq]
   388	    calc
   389	      (S - T) * (S - T) = S * S - S * T - T * S + T * T := by
   390	        noncomm_ring
   391	      _ = (2 : ℂ) • (1 : Op ι) - S * T - T * S := by
   392	        rw [hS.2, hT.2]
   393	        module
   394	  unfold stateDepDistSq
   395	  rw [hdiff]
   396	  simp only [Matrix.sub_mul, Matrix.trace_sub, Complex.sub_re]
   397	  rw [smul_mul_assoc, one_mul, Matrix.trace_smul, htrace]
   398	  norm_num [Complex.mul_re]
   399	  rw [hcross]
   400	  ring

   403	correlation. -/
   404	theorem binaryObservableDistSq_eq_one_sub_correlation
   405	    {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   406	    (S T ρ : Op ι) (hS : IsBinaryObservable S)
   407	    (hT : IsBinaryObservable T) (hρ : ρ.PosSemidef)
   408	    (htrace : Matrix.trace ρ = 1) :

   411	  rw [binaryObservableDistSq_eq_stateDepDistSq_div_two,
   412	    stateDepDistSq_eq_two_sub_two_mul_correlation S T ρ hS hT hρ htrace]

     4	/-!
     5	# The operator-valued BLR bound
     6	
     7	This file carries out the Fourier-analytic part of the proof of the quantum
     8	linearity theorem of Natarajan and Vidick.  Given binary observables `O^u`
     9	indexed by the Boolean cube `(ZMod 2)^t` and a positive semidefinite trace-one
    10	operator `ρ`, it expresses the state-dependent multiplicative defect of the
    11	family through the two-query correlation of the linearity test, identifies the
    12	sum of the cubic Fourier coefficients with that correlation, and records the
    13	overlap certificate for the Fourier-square POVM `B^u = (hat O^u)^2` that the
    14	Naimark dilation consumes.  Pairwise commutation of the observables is never
    15	assumed, and every complex trace is handled through its real part.
    16	
    17	## Main results
    18	
    19	* `multiplicativeDefect`: the state-dependent squared defect of `O^u O^v`
    20	  from `O^{u+v}`.
    21	* `avg_multiplicativeDefect_eq_two_sub_two_mul_correlation` and
    22	  `avg_multiplicativeDefect_le_two_mul_error`: the average defect equals
    23	  `2 - 2 * (correlation)`, hence is at most `2 * δ` under the correlation
    24	  hypothesis of `exists_exactly_linear_observables`.
    25	* `operatorFourier_cube_trace_eq_correlation`: the identity
    26	  `∑_u Tr_ρ((hat O^u)^3) = E_{a,b} Tr_ρ(O^a O^b O^{a+b})`.
    27	* `fourierSquareMeasurement` and `one_sub_error_le_avg_overlap_fourierSquare`:
    28	  the Fourier-square POVM together with its overlap certificate.
    29	
    30	## References
    31	
    32	Natarajan--Vidick, arXiv:1610.03574, Theorem 10 with displays (7)--(8) and
    33	its proof, `references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1074-1113`; the state-dependent
    34	distance is defined at lines 866--900 of the same file.  The QPBT paper quotes
    35	the theorem at
    36	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:711-725` and
    37	invokes it at lines 787--832.  The blueprint statement is `thm:linearity` in
    38	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:81-147`.  The normalization of
    39	the error constant is analyzed in
    40	`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_linearity-distance-normalization.tex`: the exact defect
    41	bound is `2 * δ` for the raw distance `stateDepDistSq`, equivalently `δ` for
    42	the normalized binary-observable distance.
    43	-/
    44	
    45	open scoped BigOperators Matrix MatrixOrder ComplexOrder
    46

    48

    50	open MIPStarRE.Quantum

    54	/-! ## The two-query correlation and the multiplicative defect -/
    55	
    56	/-- The two-query correlation of the linearity test: the average, over a
    57	uniformly random pair `(u, u')` in `(ZMod 2)^t`, of the real part of
    58	`Tr(O^u O^{u'} O^{u+u'} ρ)`.  This is the left-hand side of display (7) in
    59	Natarajan--Vidick, `references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1078-1080`, and the
    60	quantity bounded below in the hypothesis of
    61	`exists_exactly_linear_observables`; the order of the two uniform variables is
    62	the one used there. -/
    63	def blrCorrelation {t : ℕ} {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    64	    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (ρ : Op ι) : ℝ :=
    65	  avgOver (uniformDistribution ((Fin t → ZMod 2) × (Fin t → ZMod 2)))
    66	    (fun pair =>
    67	      (Matrix.trace (O pair.1 * O pair.2 * O (pair.1 + pair.2) * ρ)).re)
    68	
    69	/-- The state-dependent squared defect of the product `O^u O^v` from `O^{u+v}`,
    70	namely `d_ρ(O^u O^v, O^{u+v})^2` for the state-dependent distance of
    71	`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:873-875`.  Its average over uniformly random
    72	`u, v` is the approximate-linearity error of the family in the sense of the QPBT
    73	quotation `references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:713-718`,

    75	def multiplicativeDefect {t : ℕ} {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    76	    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (ρ : Op ι) (u v : Fin t → ZMod 2) : ℝ :=
    77	  stateDepDistSq (O u * O v) (O (u + v)) ρ

    79	/-- Pointwise form of the defect identity: for binary observables the squared
    80	defect of `O^u O^v` from `O^{u+v}` is `2 - 2 Re Tr(O^v O^u O^{v+u} ρ)`.  The
    81	expansion of `(O^u O^v - O^{u+v})^† (O^u O^v - O^{u+v})` produces the two
    82	triple products `O^v O^u O^{u+v}` and `O^{u+v} O^u O^v`; the second is the
    83	adjoint of the first, so their traces against `ρ` are complex conjugates with
    84	equal real parts.  This is the calculation behind display (3) of
    85	`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:900-912`, applied to the products of the
    86	family. -/
    87	theorem multiplicativeDefect_eq_two_sub_two_mul_correlation {t : ℕ}
    88	    {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    89	    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (hO : ∀ a, IsBinaryObservable (O a))
    90	    (ρ : Op ι) (hρ : ρ.PosSemidef) (htrace : ρ.trace = 1)
    91	    (u v : Fin t → ZMod 2) :
    92	    multiplicativeDefect O ρ u v =
    93	      2 - 2 * (Matrix.trace (O v * O u * O (v + u) * ρ)).re := by
    94	  have hu := hO u
    95	  have hv := hO v
    96	  have huv := hO (u + v)
    97	  have hdiff :
    98	      (O u * O v - O (u + v))ᴴ * (O u * O v - O (u + v)) =
    99	        (2 : ℂ) • (1 : Op ι) - O v * O u * O (u + v) - O (u + v) * O u * O v := by
   100	    rw [Matrix.conjTranspose_sub, Matrix.conjTranspose_mul, hu.1.eq, hv.1.eq,
   101	      huv.1.eq]
   102	    calc
   103	      (O v * O u - O (u + v)) * (O u * O v - O (u + v)) =
   104	          O v * (O u * O u) * O v - O v * O u * O (u + v) -
   105	            O (u + v) * O u * O v + O (u + v) * O (u + v) := by
   106	        noncomm_ring
   107	      _ = (2 : ℂ) • (1 : Op ι) - O v * O u * O (u + v) -
   108	            O (u + v) * O u * O v := by
   109	        rw [hu.2, Matrix.mul_one, hv.2, huv.2]
   110	        module
   111	  have hstar :
   112	      star (Matrix.trace (O (u + v) * O u * O v * ρ)) =
   113	        Matrix.trace (O v * O u * O (u + v) * ρ) := by
   114	    calc
   115	      star (Matrix.trace (O (u + v) * O u * O v * ρ)) =
   116	          Matrix.trace ((O (u + v) * O u * O v * ρ)ᴴ) := by
   117	        rw [Matrix.trace_conjTranspose]
   118	      _ = Matrix.trace (ρ * (O v * O u * O (u + v))) := by
   119	        simp [Matrix.conjTranspose_mul, hu.1.eq, hv.1.eq, huv.1.eq,
   120	          hρ.isHermitian.eq, Matrix.mul_assoc]
   121	      _ = Matrix.trace (O v * O u * O (u + v) * ρ) := by
   122	        exact Matrix.trace_mul_comm _ _
   123	  have hcross :
   124	      (Matrix.trace (O (u + v) * O u * O v * ρ)).re =
   125	        (Matrix.trace (O v * O u * O (u + v) * ρ)).re := by
   126	    have := congrArg Complex.re hstar
   127	    simpa [Complex.star_def, Complex.conj_re] using this
   128	  unfold multiplicativeDefect stateDepDistSq
   129	  rw [hdiff]
   130	  simp only [Matrix.sub_mul, Matrix.trace_sub, Complex.sub_re]
   131	  rw [smul_mul_assoc, one_mul, Matrix.trace_smul, htrace]
   132	  norm_num [Complex.mul_re]
   133	  rw [hcross, add_comm v u]
   134	  ring

   140	exchanging the two coordinates leaves the average unchanged.  This is the
   141	relation between the approximate-linearity hypothesis of the QPBT quotation
   142	(`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:713-718`) and
   143	display (7) of Natarajan--Vidick (`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1078-1080`),

   146	theorem avg_multiplicativeDefect_eq_two_sub_two_mul_correlation {t : ℕ}
   147	    {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   148	    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (hO : ∀ a, IsBinaryObservable (O a))
   149	    (ρ : Op ι) (hρ : ρ.PosSemidef) (htrace : ρ.trace = 1) :

   152	      2 - 2 * blrCorrelation O ρ := by

   154	      avgOver (uniformDistribution ((Fin t → ZMod 2) × (Fin t → ZMod 2)))

   156	          (Matrix.trace (O pair.2 * O pair.1 * O (pair.2 + pair.1) * ρ)).re) =
   157	        blrCorrelation O ρ := by
   158	    unfold blrCorrelation
   159	    refine (avgOver_uniform_equiv (Equiv.prodComm _ _) _).trans ?_
   160	    exact avgOver_congr _ _ _ (fun pair => rfl)

   162	    avgOver (uniformDistribution ((Fin t → ZMod 2) × (Fin t → ZMod 2)))
   163	        (fun pair => multiplicativeDefect O ρ pair.1 pair.2) =
   164	        avgOver (uniformDistribution ((Fin t → ZMod 2) × (Fin t → ZMod 2)))
   165	          (fun pair => 2 - 2 *
   166	            (Matrix.trace (O pair.2 * O pair.1 * O (pair.2 + pair.1) * ρ)).re) :=
   167	      avgOver_congr _ _ _ (fun pair =>
   168	        multiplicativeDefect_eq_two_sub_two_mul_correlation O hO ρ hρ htrace
   169	          pair.1 pair.2)

   171	      rw [avgOver_sub, avgOver_const_mul, avgOver_uniform_const, hswap]

   193	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma for the Fourier computations in the
   194	proof of Theorem 10 of Natarajan--Vidick
   195	(`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1096-1112`): a twisted form of the
   196	matrix-valued Parseval identity in which only the first factor is expanded
   197	through its Fourier coefficients.  Taking `a = 0` recovers Parseval. -/
   198	private theorem sum_booleanCharacter_smul_operatorFourier_mul {t : ℕ}
   199	    {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   200	    (A X : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (a : Fin t → ZMod 2) :
   201	    ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2,
   202	        booleanCharacter u a • (operatorFourier A u * X u) =
   203	      ((Fintype.card (Fin t → ZMod 2) : ℂ)⁻¹) •
   204	        ∑ b : Fin t → ZMod 2,
   205	          A b * ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2, booleanCharacter u (a + b) • X u := by
   206	  classical
   207	  let N : ℂ := Fintype.card (Fin t → ZMod 2)
   208	  calc
   209	    ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2,
   210	        booleanCharacter u a • (operatorFourier A u * X u) =
   211	        ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2, N⁻¹ • ∑ b : Fin t → ZMod 2,
   212	          booleanCharacter u (a + b) • (A b * X u) := by
   213	      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   214	      intro u _
   215	      simp only [operatorFourier, N, smul_mul_assoc, Finset.sum_mul,
   216	        Finset.smul_sum, smul_smul, booleanCharacter_add_right]
   217	      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   218	      intro b _
   219	      congr 1
   220	      ring
   221	    _ = N⁻¹ • ∑ b : Fin t → ZMod 2, ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2,
   222	          booleanCharacter u (a + b) • (A b * X u) := by
   223	      rw [← Finset.smul_sum]
   224	      congr 1
   225	      exact Finset.sum_comm
   226	    _ = N⁻¹ • ∑ b : Fin t → ZMod 2,
   227	          A b * ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2, booleanCharacter u (a + b) • X u := by
   228	      congr 1
   229	      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   230	      intro b _
   231	      rw [Finset.mul_sum]
   232	      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   233	      intro u _
   234	      rw [mul_smul_comm]
   235

236	/-- The sum of the cubes of the Fourier coefficients of an operator family is
   237	the average of `O^a O^b O^{a+b}` over a uniformly random pair `(a, b)`.  This
   238	is the operator form of the identity
   239	`∑_u (hat A^u)^3 = E_{a,b} A(a) A(b) A(a+b)` invoked at
   240	`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1111-1112`; the order of the three factors
   241	is preserved throughout. -/
   242	theorem sum_operatorFourier_cube {t : ℕ} {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   243	    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) :
   244	    ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2,
   245	        operatorFourier O u * operatorFourier O u * operatorFourier O u =
   246	      ((Fintype.card ((Fin t → ZMod 2) × (Fin t → ZMod 2)) : ℂ)⁻¹) •
   247	        ∑ p : (Fin t → ZMod 2) × (Fin t → ZMod 2),
   248	          O p.1 * O p.2 * O (p.1 + p.2) := by
   249	  classical
   250	  let N : ℂ := Fintype.card (Fin t → ZMod 2)
   251	  have hinner : ∀ b : Fin t → ZMod 2,
   252	      ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2,
   253	          booleanCharacter u b • (operatorFourier O u * operatorFourier O u) =
   254	        N⁻¹ • ∑ c : Fin t → ZMod 2, O c * O (b + c) := by
   255	    intro b
   256	    rw [sum_booleanCharacter_smul_operatorFourier_mul]
   257	    congr 1
   258	    apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   259	    intro c _
   260	    rw [operatorFourier_inversion]
   261	  calc
   262	    ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2,
   263	        operatorFourier O u * operatorFourier O u * operatorFourier O u =
   264	        ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2, booleanCharacter u 0 •
   265	          (operatorFourier O u * (operatorFourier O u * operatorFourier O u)) := by
   266	      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   267	      intro u _
   268	      rw [booleanCharacter_zero_right, one_smul, Matrix.mul_assoc]
   269	    _ = N⁻¹ • ∑ b : Fin t → ZMod 2, O b * ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2,
   270	          booleanCharacter u (0 + b) •
   271	            (operatorFourier O u * operatorFourier O u) := by
   272	      rw [sum_booleanCharacter_smul_operatorFourier_mul]
   273	    _ = N⁻¹ • ∑ b : Fin t → ZMod 2,
   274	          O b * (N⁻¹ • ∑ c : Fin t → ZMod 2, O c * O (b + c)) := by
   275	      simp only [zero_add, hinner]
   276	    _ = (N⁻¹ * N⁻¹) • ∑ b : Fin t → ZMod 2, ∑ c : Fin t → ZMod 2,
   277	          O b * O c * O (b + c) := by
   278	      simp only [mul_smul_comm, Finset.mul_sum, ← Finset.smul_sum, smul_smul,
   279	        Matrix.mul_assoc]
   280	    _ = ((Fintype.card ((Fin t → ZMod 2) × (Fin t → ZMod 2)) : ℂ)⁻¹) •
   281	          ∑ p : (Fin t → ZMod 2) × (Fin t → ZMod 2),
   282	            O p.1 * O p.2 * O (p.1 + p.2) := by
   283	      rw [Fintype.sum_prod_type, Fintype.card_prod, Nat.cast_mul, mul_inv]

     5	# Boolean Fourier analysis for the quantum linearity theorem
     6	
     7	This file develops the finite Fourier identities used in the proof of the
     8	quantum linearity theorem.  The Boolean characters are the additive characters

    11	relating the state-dependent operator distance to the distance between the

   136	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma for the Fourier transform at
   137	`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1095-1098`: orthogonality of two Boolean
   138	characters, in the form used by Fourier inversion and Parseval. -/
   139	theorem sum_booleanCharacter_mul {t : ℕ} (a b : Fin t → ZMod 2) :
   140	    ∑ u : Fin t → ZMod 2, booleanCharacter u a * booleanCharacter u b =
   141	      if a = b then (Fintype.card (Fin t → ZMod 2) : ℂ) else 0 := by
   142	  rw [← Finset.sum_congr rfl (fun u _ => booleanCharacter_add_right u a b)]
   143	  rw [sum_booleanCharacter_swap]
   144	  have hab : a + b = 0 ↔ a = b := by

   146	    · intro h
   147	      have := congrFun h
   148	      funext i
   149	      have hi := this i
   150	      exact (CharTwo.add_eq_zero.mp hi)
   151	    · intro h
   152	      subst b
   153	      ext i
   154	      exact CharTwo.add_self_eq_zero (a i)
   155	  simp only [hab]

   258	\begin{definition}[Distance between POVMs]
   259	  \label{def:povm-distance}
   260		Let $\mX$ be a finite set and $\mu$ a distribution on $\mX$. 
   261	  Let $\ket{\psi} \in \cal{H}$ be a quantum state, and for all $x\in \mX$,
   262	  $\{M^x_a\}$ and $\{N^x_a\}$ two POVMs on $\mH$.
   263	  We say that \emph{$\{M^x_a\}$ and $\{N^x_a\}$ are $\delta$-close on state
   264	    $\ket{\psi}$ and under distribution $\mu$} if
   265	  \begin{equation*}
   266	    \E_{x\sim \mu} \sum_a \norm{ (M^x_a - N^x_a) \ket{\psi} }^2 \leq O(\delta)\;,
   267	  \end{equation*}
   268	  and we write $M^x_a \approx_\delta N^x_a$ to denote this when the state
   269	  $\ket{\psi}$ and distribution $\mu$ are clear from context.
   270	  This distance is referred to as the \emph{state-dependent} distance.
   271	\end{definition}

    98	\begin{theorem}[Quantum linearity test~\cite{Natarajan2017Linearity}]
    99		\label{thm:linearity}
   100		\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.IsBinaryObservable, MIPStarRE.QPBT.stateDepDistSq}
   101		\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.exists_exactly_linear_observables}
   102		\notready
   103		\uses{def:povm-conventions}
   104		Let $t$ be a positive integer and $\delta \ge 0$. Let $\rho$ be a
   105		density operator on a Hilbert space $\hilb$ and let
   106		$\{\mathcal{O}^u\}$ be a set of binary observables indexed by
   107		$u \in \F_2^t$ acting on $\hilb$, such that on average over $u, u'$
   108		chosen uniformly at random from $\F_2^t$,
   109		\[
   110			\E_{u,u'} \Tr\big(\mathcal{O}^u \, \mathcal{O}^{u'} \,
   111			\mathcal{O}^{u+u'} \, \rho\big) \ge 1 - \delta\,.
   112		\]
   113		Then there exist a Hilbert space $\hilb'$, a pure state
   114		$\ket{\mathrm{anc}} \in \hilb'$, and binary observables
   115		$\{\mathcal{L}^u\}$ indexed by $u \in \F_2^t$ acting on
   116		$\hilb \ot \hilb'$ such that, writing
   117		$\rho' = \rho \ot \ket{\mathrm{anc}}\bra{\mathrm{anc}}$, the exact
   118		linearity
   119		\[
   120			\mathcal{L}^u \, \mathcal{L}^{u'} = \mathcal{L}^{u+u'}
   121		\]
   122		holds for all $u, u' \in \F_2^t$, and
   123		\[
   124			\E_{u} \, d_{\rho'}\big(\mathcal{L}^u,\ \mathcal{O}^u \ot
   125			\Id_{\hilb'}\big)^2 \le \delta\,,
   126		\]
   127		where the expectation is over $u$ chosen uniformly at random from
   128		$\F_2^t$ and
   129		$d_{\sigma}(S,T)
   130		= \big(\Tr\big((S-T)^\dagger (S-T)\, \sigma\big)\big)^{1/2}$
   131		denotes the state-dependent distance with respect to a density
   132		operator $\sigma$.
   133	\end{theorem}

   149	\begin{remark}[Obligations of the linearity-theorem import]
   150		\label{rem:linearity-import}
   151		Theorem~\ref{thm:linearity} is stated in the form proved in
   152		\cite{Natarajan2017Linearity}. Three features are load-bearing for the
   153		proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-4-10}: the error is preserved without
   154		polynomial loss ($\delta$ in the hypothesis becomes $\delta$ in the
   155		conclusion); the linearity of the $\{\mathcal{L}^u\}$ is exact and
   156		holds for all pairs $(u,u')$, not merely on average; and the
   157		hypothesis carries no upper bound on $\delta$, so the theorem may be
   158		applied separately for each pair $(x,z)$ with hypothesis error the
   159		conditional linearity defect given $(x,z)$, a quantity for which no a
   160		priori bound is available. The closeness of $\mathcal{L}^u$ to
   161		$\mathcal{O}^u$ is guaranteed on average over a uniformly random $u$
   162		only; this averaged form suffices because the $\mathcal{L}^u$ enter
   163		the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-4-10} only through averages over $u$.
   164		The quotation of the theorem in \cite{Ji2020MIPStar} differs from the
   165		cited statement in three respects: it inserts the restriction
   166		$0 \le \delta \le 1$, which would block the fiberwise application
   167		just described; it places the closeness conclusion, together with the
   168		exact linearity, under the quantifier ``for all $u, u' \in \F_2^t$'',
   169		a strengthening of the theorem proved in
   170		\cite{Natarajan2017Linearity}; and it appends the identity
   171		$\mathcal{L}^u = \Id$ for $u = 0$. None of the three is reproduced
   172		here: the restriction is dropped, the pointwise closeness is not
   173		used, and the appended identity is instead derived from the
   174		conclusion, since exact linearity at $u = u' = 0$ gives
   175		$(\mathcal{L}^0)^2 = \mathcal{L}^0$, and an idempotent unitary equals
   176		the identity. The import carries two conversion obligations,
   177		discharged in the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-4-10}: the theorem is
   178		instantiated with $\rho$ the reduced density operator of
   179		$\ket{\hat\psi}$ on the registers carrying the observables, so that
   180		traces against $\rho$ are expectation values in $\ket{\hat\psi}$; and
   181		the correlation hypothesis and the squared-distance conclusion are
   182		converted to and from the relation $\approx_\delta$ of
   183		Definition~\ref{def:povm-distance} by expanding the square, using
   184		unitarity of the observables, and relabelling the averaged index
   185		pair, at the cost of the constant factors absorbed by that
   186		definition. One obligation remains open and is flagged where it
   187		arises: the ancilla register $\hilb'$ and its state
   188		$\ket{\mathrm{anc}}$ produced by the theorem, which may depend on the
   189		pair $(x,z)$, must be absorbed --- uniformly in $(x,z)$ --- into
   190		zero-state padding of the strategy state, padding that the source
   191		assumes present without construction.
   192	\end{remark}

item.text: The paper-gap claim survives the convention check: QPBT’s operator `≈_δ` is the raw squared norm, while NV’s Fourier proof controls binary-measurement consistency. The four-point example correctly separates those by a factor of two, including after ancillary extension. I’m moving to API/style review now, especially whether the new private averaging and Fourier lemmas duplicate existing project or Mathlib results and whether every public declaration has the right documentation and export surface.

+/-!
+# The operator-valued BLR bound
+
+This file carries out the Fourier-analytic part of the proof of the quantum
+linearity theorem of Natarajan and Vidick.  Given binary observables `O^u`
+indexed by the Boolean cube `(ZMod 2)^t` and a positive semidefinite trace-one
+operator `ρ`, it expresses the state-dependent multiplicative defect of the
+family through the two-query correlation of the linearity test, identifies the
+sum of the cubic Fourier coefficients with that correlation, and records the
+overlap certificate for the Fourier-square POVM `B^u = (hat O^u)^2` that the
+Naimark dilation consumes.  Pairwise commutation of the observables is never
+assumed, and every complex trace is handled through its real part.
+
+## Main results
+
+* `multiplicativeDefect`: the state-dependent squared defect of `O^u O^v`
+  from `O^{u+v}`.
+* `avg_multiplicativeDefect_eq_two_sub_two_mul_correlation` and
+  `avg_multiplicativeDefect_le_two_mul_error`: the average defect equals
+  `2 - 2 * (correlation)`, hence is at most `2 * δ` under the correlation
+  hypothesis of `exists_exactly_linear_observables`.
+* `operatorFourier_cube_trace_eq_correlation`: the identity
+  `∑_u Tr_ρ((hat O^u)^3) = E_{a,b} Tr_ρ(O^a O^b O^{a+b})`.
+* `fourierSquareMeasurement` and `one_sub_error_le_avg_overlap_fourierSquare`:
+  the Fourier-square POVM together with its overlap certificate.
+
+## References
+
+Natarajan--Vidick, arXiv:1610.03574, Theorem 10 with displays (7)--(8) and
+its proof, `references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1074-1113`; the state-dependent
+distance is defined at lines 866--900 of the same file.  The QPBT paper quotes
+the theorem at
+`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:711-725` and
+invokes it at lines 787--832.  The blueprint statement is `thm:linearity` in
+`blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:81-147`.  The normalization of
+the error constant is analyzed in
+`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_linearity-distance-normalization.tex`: the exact defect
+bound is `2 * δ` for the raw distance `stateDepDistSq`, equivalently `δ` for
+the normalized binary-observable distance.
+-/
+
+open scoped BigOperators Matrix MatrixOrder ComplexOrder
+
+namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
+

+open MIPStarRE.Quantum
+
