+/-! ## The two-query correlation and the multiplicative defect -/
+
+/-- The two-query correlation of the linearity test: the average, over a
+uniformly random pair `(u, u')` in `(ZMod 2)^t`, of the real part of
+`Tr(O^u O^{u'} O^{u+u'} ρ)`.  This is the left-hand side of display (7) in
+Natarajan--Vidick, `references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1078-1080`, and the
+quantity bounded below in the hypothesis of
+`exists_exactly_linear_observables`; the order of the two uniform variables is
+the one used there. -/
+def blrCorrelation {t : ℕ} {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
+    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (ρ : Op ι) : ℝ :=
+  avgOver (uniformDistribution ((Fin t → ZMod 2) × (Fin t → ZMod 2)))
+    (fun pair =>
+      (Matrix.trace (O pair.1 * O pair.2 * O (pair.1 + pair.2) * ρ)).re)
+
+/-- The state-dependent squared defect of the product `O^u O^v` from `O^{u+v}`,
+namely `d_ρ(O^u O^v, O^{u+v})^2` for the state-dependent distance of
+`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:873-875`.  Its average over uniformly random
+`u, v` is the approximate-linearity error of the family in the sense of the QPBT
+quotation `references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:713-718`,
+measured with the raw distance `stateDepDistSq`. -/
+def multiplicativeDefect {t : ℕ} {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
+    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (ρ : Op ι) (u v : Fin t → ZMod 2) : ℝ :=
+  stateDepDistSq (O u * O v) (O (u + v)) ρ
+
+/-- Pointwise form of the defect identity: for binary observables the squared
+defect of `O^u O^v` from `O^{u+v}` is `2 - 2 Re Tr(O^v O^u O^{v+u} ρ)`.  The
+expansion of `(O^u O^v - O^{u+v})^† (O^u O^v - O^{u+v})` produces the two
+triple products `O^v O^u O^{u+v}` and `O^{u+v} O^u O^v`; the second is the
+adjoint of the first, so their traces against `ρ` are complex conjugates with
+equal real parts.  This is the calculation behind display (3) of
+`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:900-912`, applied to the products of the
+family. -/
+theorem multiplicativeDefect_eq_two_sub_two_mul_correlation {t : ℕ}
+    {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
+    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (hO : ∀ a, IsBinaryObservable (O a))
+    (ρ : Op ι) (hρ : ρ.PosSemidef) (htrace : ρ.trace = 1)
+    (u v : Fin t → ZMod 2) :
+    multiplicativeDefect O ρ u v =
+      2 - 2 * (Matrix.trace (O v * O u * O (v + u) * ρ)).re := by
+  have hu := hO u
+  have hv := hO v
+  have huv := hO (u + v)
+  have hdiff :
+      (O u * O v - O (u + v))ᴴ * (O u * O v - O (u + v)) =
+        (2 : ℂ) • (1 : Op ι) - O v * O u * O (u + v) - O (u + v) * O u * O v := by
+    rw [Matrix.conjTranspose_sub, Matrix.conjTranspose_mul, hu.1.eq, hv.1.eq,
+      huv.1.eq]
+    calc
+      (O v * O u - O (u + v)) * (O u * O v - O (u + v)) =
+          O v * (O u * O u) * O v - O v * O u * O (u + v) -
+            O (u + v) * O u * O v + O (u + v) * O (u + v) := by
+        noncomm_ring
+      _ = (2 : ℂ) • (1 : Op ι) - O v * O u * O (u + v) -
+            O (u + v) * O u * O v := by
+        rw [hu.2, Matrix.mul_one, hv.2, huv.2]
+        module
+  have hstar :
+      star (Matrix.trace (O (u + v) * O u * O v * ρ)) =
+        Matrix.trace (O v * O u * O (u + v) * ρ) := by
+    calc
+      star (Matrix.trace (O (u + v) * O u * O v * ρ)) =
+          Matrix.trace ((O (u + v) * O u * O v * ρ)ᴴ) := by
+        rw [Matrix.trace_conjTranspose]
+      _ = Matrix.trace (ρ * (O v * O u * O (u + v))) := by
+        simp [Matrix.conjTranspose_mul, hu.1.eq, hv.1.eq, huv.1.eq,
+          hρ.isHermitian.eq, Matrix.mul_assoc]
+      _ = Matrix.trace (O v * O u * O (u + v) * ρ) := by
+        exact Matrix.trace_mul_comm _ _
+  have hcross :
+      (Matrix.trace (O (u + v) * O u * O v * ρ)).re =
+        (Matrix.trace (O v * O u * O (u + v) * ρ)).re := by
+    have := congrArg Complex.re hstar
+    simpa [Complex.star_def, Complex.conj_re] using this
+  unfold multiplicativeDefect stateDepDistSq
+  rw [hdiff]
+  simp only [Matrix.sub_mul, Matrix.trace_sub, Complex.sub_re]
+  rw [smul_mul_assoc, one_mul, Matrix.trace_smul, htrace]
+  norm_num [Complex.mul_re]
+  rw [hcross, add_comm v u]
+  ring
+
+/-- The average multiplicative defect over a uniformly random pair equals
+`2 - 2 * (two-query correlation)`.  The pointwise identity
+`multiplicativeDefect_eq_two_sub_two_mul_correlation` produces the correlation
+summand with the two variables in reversed order; since the pair is uniform,
+exchanging the two coordinates leaves the average unchanged.  This is the
+relation between the approximate-linearity hypothesis of the QPBT quotation
+(`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:713-718`) and
+display (7) of Natarajan--Vidick (`references/nv-paper/fullpaper.tex:1078-1080`),
+in the raw normalization of
+`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_linearity-distance-normalization.tex`. -/
+theorem avg_multiplicativeDefect_eq_two_sub_two_mul_correlation {t : ℕ}
+    {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
+    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι) (hO : ∀ a, IsBinaryObservable (O a))
+    (ρ : Op ι) (hρ : ρ.PosSemidef) (htrace : ρ.trace = 1) :
+    avgOver (uniformDistribution ((Fin t → ZMod 2) × (Fin t → ZMod 2)))
+        (fun pair => multiplicativeDefect O ρ pair.1 pair.2) =
+      2 - 2 * blrCorrelation O ρ := by
+  have hswap :
+      avgOver (uniformDistribution ((Fin t → ZMod 2) × (Fin t → ZMod 2)))
+        (fun pair =>
+          (Matrix.trace (O pair.2 * O pair.1 * O (pair.2 + pair.1) * ρ)).re) =
+        blrCorrelation O ρ := by
+    unfold blrCorrelation
+    refine (avgOver_uniform_equiv (Equiv.prodComm _ _) _).trans ?_
+    exact avgOver_congr _ _ _ (fun pair => rfl)

    12	
    13	### Linter warnings
    14	
    15	Do not mask linter warnings instead of fixing them. A cleanup PR should not add
    16	broad `set_option linter.<name> false` blocks, and especially not file-wide
    17	blocks, just to make the build output quieter. Linters exist to expose real
    18	maintenance problems; hiding them makes later proof work and review harder.
    19	
    20	Fix the warning at its source whenever possible:
    21	
    22	- wrap long lines rather than disabling `linter.style.longLine`;
    23	- remove or narrow unused variables, section variables, and unused typeclass
    24	  assumptions rather than disabling the corresponding unused-* linter;
    25	- remove unused `simp` arguments rather than disabling `linter.unusedSimpArgs`;
    26	- rewrite proof terms or state the simplified goal explicitly rather than
    27	  silencing `linter.flexible`.
    28	
    29	If a linter warning is a genuine false positive or a temporary porting
    30	exception, use the narrowest possible scope, preferably
    31	`set_option linter.<name> false in <decl>`, and add a short nearby explanation.
    32	Such exceptions should be rare and reviewable. Never use linter suppression as
    33	the main mechanism for a linter-warning cleanup PR.
    34	
    35	## PR review (MATHLIB_pr-review)
    36	
    37	### Source-faithfulness checks
    38	
    39	For this repository, the first review question is whether a paper-facing Lean
    40	statement still represents the cited result in `references/ldt-paper/`.  Before
    41	applying the general mathlib review checklist in the lean-conventions
    42	`MATHLIB_pr-review` reference, compare every changed
    43	source-labelled theorem, lemma, proposition, corollary, or definition with the
    44	corresponding paper statement and the active blueprint entry.
    45	
    46	Reject a paper-facing statement if it has acquired a non-paper bridge, residual,
    47	repair, package, producer, proof-obligation, assumptions-bundle, hypotheses-bundle,
    48	or arbitrary implication hypothesis.  Necessary boundary hypotheses, such as
    49	positivity for division or nonemptiness of a finite type, may be faithful formal
    50	encodings of implicit paper assumptions, but they should be documented when
    51	mathematically load-bearing.
    52	
    53	Reviewers should also inspect `\lean{}` and `\leanok` links.  A source-labelled
    54	blueprint entry should point to the source theorem or its faithful construction
    55	theorem, not to conditional helpers whose assumptions are proof obligations.
    56	Auxiliary Lean declarations may be recorded in a separate remark, provided the
    57	remark states that they are not additional hypotheses in the paper theorem.

    68	> witnesses, Mathlib-bypass castles, external `*Statement` smuggles).
    69	> Consult it alongside this file during review.
    70	
    71	### Project paper-realignment protocol
    72	
    73	The canonical paper-realignment exception in the lean-conventions
    74	`PROOF_INTEGRITY` reference is instantiated here as
    75	follows (the protocol and the `**Unfaithful:**` marker are described in
    76	`AGENTS.md`):
    77	
    78	> **Paper-realignment exception:** When a PR is explicitly realigning a
    79	> source-labelled declaration with `references/ldt-paper/`, the `sorry`
    80	> blocker of the lean-conventions `PROOF_INTEGRITY` reference may be
    81	> temporarily relaxed for the affected proof bodies.  The
    82	> PR must restore the source-faithful public statement, name the remaining proof
    83	> obligation as a theorem or lemma, and cite the paper passage plus the
    84	> tracking issue or paper-gap note.  A theorem whose proof still depends on a
    85	> known non-paper bridge, residual, repair input, obligation structure, or
    86	> conditional helper
    87	> must carry the `**Unfaithful:**` docstring marker described in `AGENTS.md`.
    88	> Review such PRs against statement faithfulness and the documented discharge
    89	> plan, not merely against the temporary `sorry` count.
    90	
    91	### Axiom policy
    92	
    93	When an external mathematical result must remain unformalized temporarily,
    94	prefer a caller-supplied `Prop` hypothesis over a global `axiom`
    95	declaration, and add a regression check (for example a
    96	`Lean.collectAxioms`-based assertion, as in
    97	`MIPStarRE.LDT.Test.AxiomAudit`) so later refactors cannot silently widen
    98	the axiomatic base.
    99	
   100	This preference does not license proposition inputs on source-labelled paper
   101	theorems.  If the cited paper theorem does not assume the proposition, a
   102	caller-supplied `Prop` hypothesis is an additional theorem hypothesis, not a
   103	proof of the paper statement.  Use such hypotheses only for explicitly
   104	conditional auxiliary results, and keep the source-labelled theorem statement
   105	faithful to the paper.
   106	
   107	### Scaffolding that blocks real formalization
   108	
   109	This is a subtle but critical failure mode: **scaffolding definitions or
   110	theorem statements that do not faithfully represent the actual mathematics**,
   111	making them impossible to connect to real Mathlib-based proofs.
   112	
   113	Signs to watch for:
   114	
   115	- Custom type definitions for objects that already exist in Mathlib (e.g.,
   116	  defining a custom `Measurement` type instead of using Mathlib's
   117	  `MeasureTheory` or operator algebra API)
   118	- Theorem statements whose hypotheses or conclusions use project-local types
   119	  that are not definitionally equal to or coercible from the Mathlib versions
   120	- Scaffolded definitions that compile but encode the wrong mathematical
   121	  semantics (e.g., a "projective measurement" definition that does not enforce
   122	  the correct positivity or completeness conditions)
   123	- Intermediate lemmas stated in terms of scaffolding types that cannot be
   124	  connected upstream to Mathlib's API without reproving everything
   125	- Definitions that "work" for `sorry`-based proofs but fail when you try to
   126	  fill in real proofs using Mathlib lemmas (type mismatches, missing instances,
   127	  incompatible universes)
   128	
   129	When reviewing scaffolded code, ask: **Can a real proof be built on top of
   130	this?** If the types, instances, and API surface don't align with Mathlib, the
   131	scaffolding is actively harmful — it creates technical debt that blocks
   132	progress rather than enabling it.
   133	
   134	### Paper-labelled theorem statement drift
   135	
   136	A theorem advertised as the Lean formalization of a paper theorem is a blocker
   137	if its public statement has drifted from the cited paper statement.
   138	Changing a theorem away from the statement in `references/ldt-paper/` is
   139	strongly discouraged unless it is forced by faithful formal encoding or by a
   140	documented mathematical necessity.
   141	
   142	The most common failure mode is replacing an unformalized proof step by an
   143	extra hypothesis on the theorem itself.  This produces a true conditional
   144	theorem, but it is not the theorem stated in the paper.  In particular, do not
   145	repair a theorem such as `mainFormal` by adding assumptions named
   146	`BridgeHypotheses`, `Input`, `Residual`, `Package`, `RepairInput`, `Producer`,
   147	generic `Hypotheses` or `Assumptions` bundles, or similar, unless those
   148	assumptions are explicitly present in the cited paper statement.
   149	
   150	Conditional helpers are a last-resort quarantine for proof work that cannot yet
   151	be closed.  Before introducing one, state the missing intermediate fact as a
   152	named lemma or theorem to be proved from the paper hypotheses.  A conditional
   153	helper is permitted only when it has a paper-gap note or tracking issue, a named
   154	obligation-discharger target, and an explicit removal plan.  Its name must show
   155	that it is conditional, for example with `_of_...`, `_assuming_...`, or
   156	`conditional...`.  It must not be the declaration used by a source-labelled
   157	blueprint theorem with `\leanok`.
   158	
   159	Existing bridge hypotheses should be treated as proof debt.  Mine their proofs
   160	for reusable arguments, but do not keep a paper-labelled theorem in a
   161	strengthened form merely because the conditional version compiles.  If the
   162	bridge data cannot be derived from the paper hypotheses, the correct repair is
   163	to restore the paper-aligned theorem statement and leave the missing proof as a
   164	tracked `sorry`, rather than to keep the extra assumption on the theorem.
   165	
   166	Not every explicit Lean hypothesis is statement drift.  Side conditions needed
   167	to encode the paper's domain, such as nonemptiness, decidability, field-model
   168	instances, positivity of parameters, or denominator nonvanishing, may be
   169	faithful when the paper uses the corresponding objects without comment.  These
   170	conditions should still be reviewed.  The issue is whether the hypothesis is
   171	mathematical domain data implicit in the source, or an unproved intermediate
   172	step of the source proof.
   173	
   174	For every paper-labelled theorem change, require a statement integrity audit:
   175	
   176	- paper assumptions versus Lean assumptions;
   177	- paper conclusion versus Lean conclusion;
   178	- verdict: exact, faithful boundary hypotheses, extra assumptions, weakened
   179	  conclusion, or strengthened conclusion.
   180	
   181	### Source-statement proof gaps
   182	
   183	**For source-statement proof gaps**: Read
   184	[`paper-gaps/proof-gap-protocol.tex`](paper-gaps/proof-gap-protocol.tex) when a
   185	proof is blocked by a bridge, residual, repair, input, package, or obligation
   186	structure.  It explains when to introduce an internal obligation theorem, why
   187	conditional helpers are exceptional temporary quarantine objects, and why a
   188	tracked `sorry` is preferable to a strengthened source theorem statement.

1	# Mathematical Language Guidelines
     2	
     3	MIPStarRE Lean names and documentation should be written for readers comparing
     4	the formalization with the paper and blueprint.
     5	
     6	This is a project-local supplement to the Mathlib-derived documentation,
     7	naming, and style guides in the lean-conventions skill's `MATHLIB_doc`,
     8	`MATHLIB_naming`, and `MATHLIB_style` references.
     9	
    10	## Scope
    11	
    12	These guidelines apply to:
    13	
    14	- public Lean declaration names and namespace names;
    15	- module docstrings;
    16	- declaration docstrings;
    17	- documentation-visible section comments;
    18	- explanatory comments that describe the mathematical role of a declaration.
    19	- blueprint prose and formalization-support notes;
    20	- issue titles and issue bodies;
    21	- PR titles and PR descriptions.
    22	
    23	## Source of Truth
    24	
    25	Use terminology from the following sources, in this order:
    26	
    27	1. `references/ldt-paper/`
    28	2. `blueprint/src/chapter/`
    29	3. established local conventions in nearby Lean files
    30	
    31	When the paper has a term for the object, use that term. For Section 5, for
    32	example, prefer orthogonalization lemma, truncation function, rounding to
    33	projectors, rank reduction, and completing to measurement.
    34	
    35	## Reference Notation And Terminology
    36	
    37	The notation and terminology of the original reference are the default for
    38	reader-facing mathematical text.  A reader should be able to compare a Lean
    39	docstring, blueprint paragraph, issue, or PR description with the cited source
    40	without first learning a private vocabulary used by the formalization.
    41	
    42	When Lean must use a different name or representation, define the deviation in a
    43	location which future readers can find from the affected statement.  Use the
    44	first applicable location in the following order:
    45	
    46	1. the declaration docstring of the public object whose name or representation
    47	   differs from the paper;
    48	2. the module docstring of the defining Lean file, when the deviation concerns a
    49	   family of declarations in that file;
    50	3. the relevant blueprint paragraph, when the notation appears only in the
    51	   blueprint;
    52	4. a report under `docs/reports/` or `docs/paper-gaps/`, when the deviation is a
    53	   larger discrepancy between the paper, blueprint, and Lean.
    54	
    55	The explanation should say:
    56	
    57	- the notation or term used in the paper;
    58	- the Lean object or name which represents it;
    59	- the mathematical reason for the difference, if there is one;
    60	- the scope in which the replacement should be used.
    61	
    62	A PR description may mention the deviation, but it should not be the only place
    63	where future readers can learn it.
    64	
    65	Formalization-only auxiliary lemmas should be introduced as such.  Their prose
    66	should name the nearby paper equation, theorem, or construction they support,
    67	rather than presenting the auxiliary name as paper terminology.
    68	
    69	## Naming Norm
    70	
    71	Names and prose should describe the mathematical object, hypothesis, or
    72	conclusion. They should not encode the history of how the formalization was
    73	assembled.
    74	
    75	Avoid presenting words such as `pipeline`, `wrapper`, `package`, `raw`,
    76	`oneShot`, or `liveBlock` as mathematical terminology unless the cited source
    77	uses them with that meaning. Likewise, avoid implementation-local substitutes
    78	such as `projectivization` or `spectral truncation` when the paper gives a
    79	clearer phrase.
    80	
    81	This is a general rule for the repository, not only a rule for file splits.
    82	Module names, namespace names, public declarations, theorem fields, docstrings,
    83	blueprint-facing names, issue titles, and spec documents should name the
    84	mathematical layer under discussion, not the local workflow step, paper line
    85	number, or implementation history.
    86	
    87	### Concrete examples
    88	
    89	The table below illustrates the naming norm with examples patterned on the
    90	codebase and on names seen during review.  Some entries are existing names;
    91	others are proposed names for future refactors.  The "avoid" column lists
    92	process-shaped names that encode the history of how the formalization was
    93	assembled; the "prefer" column lists mathematical names that a reader of the
    94	paper or blueprint would recognize.
    95	
    96	| Avoid (process-shaped)                        | Prefer (mathematical)                     | Rationale                                              |
    97	|:----------------------------------------------|:------------------------------------------|:-------------------------------------------------------|
    98	| `Line130`                                     | `ProjectiveConsistency`                   | Paper Lemma 5.13, not "the line-130 identity"          |
    99	| `Line169`                                     | `CompletionTransport`                     | Paper Lemma 5.16, step that transports completed data  |
   100	| `Step6`                                       | `Orthonormalization`                      | Paper Section 5, the orthonormalization construction   |
   101	| `FinalAssembly`                               | `DiagonalCompletion`                      | Paper Lemma 5.17, constructing a diagonal POVM         |
   102	| `OneShotIneq`                                 | `SelfConsistencyDataProcessing` (or existing module `Preliminaries.SelfConsistency.DataProcessing`)           | Paper's data-processing inequality for self-consistency |
   103	| `PipelineCheck`                               | `ErrorPropagationBound` (proposed)                   | The bound that propagates error through the test       |
   104	| `QxpLayerWrapper`                             | `ProjectivePOVMCompletion` (proposed)                | The construction from round-projectors to POVMs        |
   105	| `RawSpectralTruncation`                       | `SpectralTruncation`                      | The paper's spectral truncation, not an "unwrapped" version |
   106	| `AddInUStep3To5`                              | `AddInUUpperExcessMass` (proposed)                  | Paper Addendum in §U, the upper excess-mass estimate   |
   107	| `AddInUStep12`                                | `AddInUCommutationTail` (proposed)                   | Paper Addendum in §U, the commutation tail estimate    |
   108	
   109	An avoided name is acceptable only when the cited paper itself uses that
   110	phrase as the mathematical name (e.g., a lemma the paper calls "Step 2").
   111	In that case the docstring should cite the paper's phrasing.
   112	
   113	File-split PRs are a common place where this rule matters: new leaves should be
   114	named by the mathematical boundary they isolate, and any public declarations
   115	exposed by the split should be reviewed under the same standard.
   116	
   117	### Shared helpers
   118	
   119	When the same (or nearly the same) helper declaration appears in two or
   120	more chapter-local leaves, the copies should be consolidated into a single
   121	shared helper in an appropriate common module.  This avoids duplication and
   122	ensures that fixes, generalizations, or upstream replacements apply to all
   123	call sites at once.  Issue [#1145] tracks this work across the repository.
   124	
   125	Procedure:
   126	
   127	1. **Confirm equivalence.**  Compare the statement of each copy.  If the
   128	   types differ only by a chapter-specific parameterization (e.g.,
   129	   `SubMeas (Polynomial params) ι` vs `SubMeas (Point params) ι`),
   130	   parameterize the shared helper over that type via a `variable` or
   131	   explicit argument.
   132	2. **Find the right home.**  Prefer a module that is already imported by
   133	   both call sites.  Typical candidates:
   134	   - `MIPStarRE/LDT/Basic/` for parameter-free operators and bounds,
   135	   - `MIPStarRE/LDT/Preliminaries/` for polynomial/field/character lemmas,
   136	   - The highest chapter that is a common dependency of the two sites.
   137	3. **Name mathematically.**  Give the shared helper a name that describes
   138	   what it states, not which chapter it originally came from.
   139	4. **Replace call sites.**  Delete the chapter-local copies and replace
   140	   their uses with the shared helper.  A thin wrapper is allowed only when it
   141	   preserves a paper-facing or blueprint-facing name that external readers
   142	   need to search for; such wrappers should have a docstring or compatibility
   143	   comment explaining why the alias exists.  Remove the wrapper once that
   144	   paper-facing name is no longer needed for external reference.
   145	5. **Document.**  Add a docstring to the shared helper citing the paper or
   146	   blueprint location it supports.
   147	
   148	### Legacy identifier treatment
   149	
   150	If a docstring must mention a legacy Lean identifier, cite it in backticks and
   151	describe the mathematical object in paper terminology. If an old public
   152	identifier cannot be renamed in the current PR, record the required migration
   153	in the issue, PR description, or an audit file under `audits/`.
   154	
   155	Do not add an empty pass-through abbreviation merely to introduce a second
   156	public name.  This is different from a documented public wrapper allowed in the
   157	shared-helper procedure above: a wrapper must preserve a paper-facing or
   158	blueprint-facing term and must say why the alias exists.
   159	
   160	## Review Checklist
   161	
   162	Reviewers should use this checklist when examining public names and
   163	documentation prose.  Flag any item that fails.
   164	
   165	- [ ] **Naming.**  Do public declaration names, namespace names, module names,
   166	      theorem field names, and docstring prose describe a mathematical object,
   167	      hypothesis, or conclusion?  Or do they encode the history of how the
   168	      formalization was assembled (paper line numbers, workflow steps,
   169	      implementation-phase labels)?
   170	- [ ] **Source alignment.**  For the mathematical content under review, does
   171	      the prose use the terminology in `references/ldt-paper/` or the
   172	      blueprint?  Are process words such as `pipeline`, `wrapper`, `package`,
   173	      `raw`, `oneShot`, or `liveBlock` used as mathematical terms when the
   174	      source does not use them that way?
   175	- [ ] **Deviation documented.**  If a Lean name or representation differs from
   176	      the paper, is the deviation documented in a declaration docstring,
   177	      module docstring, blueprint paragraph, or `docs/paper-gaps/` note, in
   178	      that order of preference?
   179	- [ ] **Auxiliary lemmas.**  Are formalization-only auxiliary lemmas introduced
   180	      as such, with prose naming the nearby paper equation, theorem, or
   181	      construction they support?
   182	- [ ] **Shared helpers.**  Does the PR introduce a helper that already exists
   183	      (or near-exists) in another chapter-local leaf?  If so, has it been
   184	      consolidated into a common module with a mathematical name?
   185	- [ ] **Legacy IDs.**  If a legacy Lean identifier is mentioned, is the
   186	      mathematical object described in paper terminology?  If an old public
   187	      identifier cannot be renamed yet, is the required migration recorded in
   188	      the issue, PR description, or an audit file?
   189	- [ ] **Pass-through names.**  Does the PR add an empty pass-through
   190	      abbreviation that introduces a second public name without adding
   191	      mathematical content?  Reject it unless it is a documented compatibility
   192	      wrapper preserving paper-facing or blueprint-facing terminology.
   193	
   194	Review-fix PRs touching a surface covered by an active audit should read the
   195	relevant audit before changing names or prose.

    16	
    17	\section{Purpose}
    18	
    19	This note fixes terminology for a recurring failure mode in the formalization
    20	of the low individual degree test paper, \path{arXiv:2009.12982}.  It
    21	complements the note-writing policy in \path{docs/paper-gaps/policy.tex} and
    22	the source-statement audit tracked historically in \ghissue{1458}.  The current
    23	source-boundary proof holes are tracked in \ghissue{1507} and \ghissue{422}.
    24	A proof may be blocked at
    25	an intermediate mathematical assertion.  If that assertion is added as a new
    26	hypothesis to a theorem labelled as a paper theorem, the resulting \Lean{}
    27	theorem
    28	may be correct as a conditional statement, but it is no longer the theorem in
    29	the cited source.  The apparent proof has not closed the paper theorem; it has
    30	moved a proof obligation into the theorem statement.
    31	
    32	The protocol below distinguishes such proof debt from legitimate formal
    33	boundary conditions and from genuine mathematical corrections.  It is meant for
    34	contributors and reviewers who must decide whether a bridge, residual, repair,
    35	input, or obligation structure is a proved local construction, a tracked proof
    36	gap, or statement drift which must be repaired before a theorem may be
    37	advertised as a source theorem.  The default rule is restrictive: such data
    38	must not be added to a paper-facing theorem unless it is part of the cited
    39	source statement or a documented faithful encoding of its ambient hypotheses.
    40	
    41	\section{Basic objects}
    42	
    43	\paragraph{Source theorem.}
    44	A source theorem is a theorem, lemma, proposition, or corollary in the paper
    45	source under \path{references/ldt-paper/}.  Its hypotheses and conclusion are
    46	the mathematical ground truth, subject only to faithful formal encoding and to
    47	documented paper-gap corrections.
    48	
    49	\paragraph{Paper-facing declaration.}
    50	A \Lean{} declaration is paper-facing when it is named or cited as the
    51	formalization of a source theorem, for instance through a blueprint
    52	\verb|\lean{}| link on a theorem environment carrying a paper label.  Such a
    53	declaration must match the source theorem in its public statement.  In
    54	particular, it may not add an unproved bridge, residual, repair, input,
    55	obligation structure, or other proof-obligation hypothesis which the paper does
    56	not assume.
    57	
    58	\paragraph{Proof obligation.}
    59	A proof obligation is an intermediate assertion needed by the proof of a source
    60	theorem.  It may be a construction, an estimate, a transport lemma, or a
    61	comparison between two formal representations.  If the paper proves or invokes
    62	this assertion, then the formalization should state it as a separate lemma or
    63	theorem and prove it from the upstream hypotheses.
    64	
    65	\paragraph{Obligation discharger.}
    66	An obligation discharger is a theorem or definition which constructs a proof
    67	obligation from the paper hypotheses already available at that point in the
    68	argument.  This is the preferred representation of missing work.  If the proof
    69	is not yet complete, the discharger may temporarily contain a tracked
    70	\verb|sorry|, but the paper-facing theorem should call it rather than assume
    71	its output as an additional theorem hypothesis.
    72	
    73	\paragraph{Conditional helper.}
    74	A conditional helper is a separately named theorem whose statement explicitly
    75	assumes a proof obligation.  Names such as
    76	\leanid{mainFormal\_ofInternalObligations},
    77	\leanid{orthonormalization\_ofInput}, or names whose suffix advertises the
    78	assumed obligation are permitted only when the declaration is not presented as
    79	the source theorem.  A conditional helper is a quarantine for downstream proof
    80	content; it does not close the source theorem.
    81	
    82	\section{Bridge, residual, repair, input, and obligation structures}
    83	
    84	The words \emph{bridge}, \emph{residual}, \emph{repair}, \emph{input}, and
    85	\emph{obligation structure} name possible formal shapes.  They become dangerous
    86	when their mathematical status is unclear or when their names make unproved
    87	data look like acceptable hypotheses of a source theorem.
    88	
    89	\paragraph{Bridge.}
    90	A bridge should be a transport theorem between two already defined
    91	mathematical forms: for example, a tensor-placement identity, a conversion
    92	between two equivalent consistency relations, or a statement translating a
    93	source object into a formal representation.  A bridge is harmless only after it
    94	is proved from previously available assumptions.  It becomes proof debt when it
    95	is assumed because the transport has not yet been proved.  It becomes theorem
    96	drift when the assumed bridge is added to a paper-facing theorem.
    97	
    98	\paragraph{Residual.}
    99	A residual is a named remainder after part of an argument has been performed.
   100	It is often a useful way to record the exact missing target after a completed
   101	construction.  A residual may appear as the conclusion of a helper theorem or
   102	as the input of a quarantined conditional helper.  It is not a permissible new
   103	assumption on a paper theorem unless the paper itself assumes that residual.
   104	
   105	\paragraph{Input.}
   106	An input is a named bundle of data or hypotheses consumed by a construction or
   107	conditional helper.  It is harmless only when each load-bearing field is either
   108	part of the source hypotheses or is produced by an earlier theorem.  It becomes
   109	proof debt when the bundle is merely assumed because the construction of its
   110	fields is missing.  It becomes theorem drift when such a bundle is added to the
   111	public statement of a source theorem.
   112	
   113	\paragraph{Repair.}
   114	A repair is a mathematical construction which replaces an approximate or
   115	partial object by a better object, usually with a quantitative estimate.  In
   116	the low individual degree test formalization, projectivization and
   117	orthonormalization repairs are genuine mathematical operations.  A repair
   118	should therefore appear as a construction or as a theorem discharging the
   119	corresponding obligation.  If a theorem assumes the output of the repair instead
   120	of constructing it, that theorem is conditional on the repair.
   121	
   122	\paragraph{Obligation structure.}
   123	An obligation structure is a record whose fields are the data and estimates
   124	needed by a later construction.  This is acceptable only as an internal target
   125	or as a hypothesis of a conditional helper.  Such a structure becomes statement
   126	drift if it is added to a paper-facing theorem instead of being constructed
   127	inside the proof.  The review question is whether every load-bearing field is
   128	proved from the source hypotheses or is explicitly tracked as a missing
   129	obligation.
   130	
   131	\section{The main failure mode}
   132	
   133	Suppose the paper proves
   134	\[
   135	  H \Longrightarrow C.
   136	\]
   137	During formalization, the proof may need an intermediate assertion \(B\).  The
   138	paper theorem should be represented as
   139	\[
   140	  H \Longrightarrow B \Longrightarrow C
   141	  \quad\text{inside the proof,}
   142	\]
   143	where \(B\) is obtained by a lemma or theorem from \(H\).  The following
   144	public statement is a different theorem:
   145	\[
   146	  H \land B \Longrightarrow C.
   147	\]
   148	It is not unsound in \Lean{}, but it is not the paper theorem.  It says that the
   149	conclusion follows if the missing bridge data is supplied.  Such a theorem is a
   150	conditional helper, even if its conclusion looks exactly like the paper's
   151	conclusion.
   152	
   153	This is the situation colloquially described as ``adding a bridge
   154	hypothesis''.  More precisely, an unproved intermediate step has been promoted
   155	from the proof body to the theorem's assumptions.  The correction is not to hide
   156	the hypothesis under a different structure name.  The correction is to keep a
   157	paper-facing theorem with the source statement and move the missing step to a
   158	named internal proof obligation.
   159	
   160	\section{Faithful boundary hypotheses}
   161	
   162	Not every extra formal hypothesis is a theorem drift.  Some hypotheses are
   163	faithful boundary conditions introduced by formal encoding.  Examples include
   164	nonnegativity needed for a real power, positivity needed to divide by a
   165	quantity, finiteness and nonemptiness of an index type, a field-model instance,
   166	or decidability instances required by \Lean{}.  Such hypotheses are acceptable
   167	when they express part of the mathematical ambient setting or make explicit a
   168	condition used implicitly in the paper.
   169	
   170	The distinction is load-bearing.  A faithful boundary hypothesis describes the
   171	domain in which the paper's objects live.  A proof-debt hypothesis supplies a
   172	mathematical step that the proof should derive.  If removing the hypothesis
   173	leaves an unproved construction or estimate from the paper proof, then the
   174	hypothesis is proof debt, not a boundary condition.
   175	
   176	\section{Definition drift and subtree repair}
   177	
   178	Definition drift is especially dangerous because it propagates.  If a
   179	definition is changed so that it no longer denotes the object in the paper,
   180	then every downstream theorem using that definition may continue to compile
   181	while proving statements about the wrong object.  Downstream theorem statements
   182	can then be repaired piecemeal, but the development remains unstable because
   183	the wrong definition is still upstream.
   184	
   185	When a definition mismatch is found, the repair should proceed by a subtree
   186	protocol.
   187	
   188	\begin{enumerate}
   189	  \item Identify the source object and the formal object precisely.
   190	  \item Freeze a source-faithful definition or state an adapter theorem
   191	  relating the existing definition to the source object.
   192	  \item Recheck the downstream theorem chain against that definition or adapter.
   193	  \item Re-formalize the affected subtree from the corrected interface, rather
   194	  than adding local hypotheses to each downstream theorem.
   195	  \item If a downstream proof cannot be completed, record the missing obligation
   196	  at the lowest point where the paper proof needs it.
   197	\end{enumerate}
   198	
   199	This is slower than editing a final theorem signature, but it prevents a local
   200	definition error from becoming a global theorem-statement error.
   201	
   202	\section{Allowed shapes}
   203	
   204	\begin{center}
   205	\begin{tabular}{p{0.24\linewidth}p{0.31\linewidth}p{0.32\linewidth}}
   206	\textbf{Shape} & \textbf{Allowed use} & \textbf{Forbidden use} \\
   207	\hline
   208	Paper-facing theorem & Matches the source statement up to faithful encoding &
   209	Carries non-paper bridge, residual, repair, input, obligation-structure, or
   210	proof-obligation hypotheses \\
   211	Source-shaped theorem with a tracked \verb|sorry| & Default repair when the
   212	source proof is blocked but the statement is known & Replaced by a strengthened
   213	theorem statement merely to keep the file compiling \\
   214	Conditional helper & Temporary quarantine for substantial proof content whose
   215	remaining named obligation has not yet been discharged & Introduced merely to
   216	avoid a \verb|sorry|, or linked as the source theorem or marked as
   217	proof-complete for that theorem \\
   218	Obligation discharger theorem & Constructs the obligation from paper hypotheses &
   219	Merely restates the obligation as an assumption \\
   220	Input bundle & Collects produced data for a local construction & Is assumed by a
   221	source theorem instead of being produced \\
   222	Obligation structure & Bundles constructed data and estimates & Hides unproved
   223	fields that are then assumed by a source theorem \\
   224	Paper-gap note & Documents a real mathematical or formal-statement divergence &
   225	Justifies silent statement drift without a repair plan
   226	\end{tabular}
   227	\end{center}
   228	
   229	\section{Protocol for a blocked proof}
   230	
   231	When a source-labelled proof is blocked, use the following order.
   232	
   233	\begin{enumerate}
   234	  \item Read the cited source statement and the proof passage in
   235	  \path{references/ldt-paper/}.
   236	  \item Write the paper theorem form, the current \Lean{} theorem form, and the
   237	  first missing intermediate assertion.
   238	  \item Decide whether the missing assertion is a faithful boundary condition,
   239	  a representation adapter, an ordinary lemma from the paper proof, or a real
   240	  paper-gap discrepancy.
   241	  \item If it is an ordinary lemma or adapter, create a named theorem which
   242	  discharges that obligation.  Do not add it to the source theorem as a new
   243	  hypothesis.
   244	  \item Keep the source-labelled theorem itself in the source form, even if its
   245	  proof must contain a tracked \verb|sorry|.  This is the default repair when
   246	  the missing assertion has not yet been proved.
   247	  \item Create a conditional helper only to quarantine substantial proof content
   248	  that already exists and would otherwise be lost.  Do not create such a helper
   249	  merely to avoid a \verb|sorry| or to keep making progress.  If a conditional
   250	  helper remains, give it a conditional name, keep it separate from the
   251	  paper-facing theorem, and record the obligation discharger that must eliminate
   252	  it.
   253	  \item If the source and formal statements genuinely differ, write or update a
   254	  note under \path{docs/paper-gaps/} before marking the statement as aligned.
   255	  \item Update the blueprint so that paper labels point only to paper-facing
   256	  declarations.  Conditional helpers belong in remarks or implementation
   257	  notes, not in the source theorem block.
   258	\end{enumerate}
   259	
   260	\section{Retirement criterion}
   261	
   262	An auxiliary declaration should be removed from the main blueprint route, or
   263	renamed and documented as a purely internal lemma, when all three of the
   264	following conditions hold:
   265	\begin{enumerate}
   266	  \item it is not a statement in the cited paper and is not an explicitly cited
   267	        outside result;
   268	  \item no current proof of a paper-level target needs it as stated;
   269	  \item it assumes stronger proof data, finite-length data, completion data,
   270	        repair data, synchronization data, or package fields than the paper
   271	        proof requires.
   272	\end{enumerate}
   273	If such a declaration is still useful as a formal intermediate result, it
   274	should remain a lemma or a visibly conditional helper with a planned discharge.
   275	It should not be a headline replacement for the paper theorem, and it should
   276	not support a source-labelled blueprint \verb|\leanok| claim.
   277	
   278	\section{Review questions}
   279	
   280	A reviewer should first compare every paper-labelled declaration with the cited
   281	source statement, checking both hypotheses and conclusion up to faithful formal
   282	encoding.  Bridge, residual, repair, input, obligation-structure, and
   283	proof-obligation assumptions should be absent from paper-facing theorem
   284	signatures unless they occur in the paper.  If a conditional helper remains,
   285	its name should be explicitly conditional and it should not support a source
   286	theorem \verb|\leanok| claim.
   287	Each load-bearing obligation-structure or input field should have a theorem
   288	discharging it, a tracked issue, or an explicit \verb|sorry| at the obligation
   289	site.  When a definition has changed, the downstream subtree should be checked
   290	against the corrected definition rather than patched locally.  Finally, if the
   291	formal statement genuinely differs from the source statement, a paper-gap note
   292	should explain the mathematical difference and give a plan to remove or justify
   293	it.
   294	
   295	\section{Conclusion}
   296	
   297	The project should prefer visible proof obligations over invisible statement
   298	drift.  A tracked \verb|sorry| in the source-shaped theorem, or in the lowest
   299	named internal obligation needed by its proof, is less misleading than a source
   300	theorem whose assumptions have been strengthened.  Conditional helpers are not a

    16	
    17	\section{Purpose}
    18	
    19	When a formalization relies on a cited mathematical source, the cited source
    20	should remain intact.  It is a source, not an errata file.  If a possible gap,
    21	missing hypothesis, incorrect numerical constant, or other mathematical
    22	discrepancy is found, the matter should be recorded in a separate LaTeX note.
    23	In this repository such notes live under \path{docs/paper-gaps/}.  The same
    24	principle applies when the formal development has already diverged from the
    25	cited source, for instance by changing a statement so that it compiles, or by
    26	using a different mathematical route because an available formal-library theorem
    27	has a slightly different form.  Such a note is a mathematical note first, and a
    28	record of the formalization second: it should be readable by a mathematician or
    29	mathematical physicist who has not followed the issue discussion.
    30	
    31	The note should isolate the mathematical mechanism.  It should say what the
    32	cited source asserts, what the cited results actually imply, where a term or
    33	hypothesis is lost, and what statement the formal development proves instead.
    34	If the formal proof takes a different route, the note should explain the
    35	replacement argument and the hypotheses on which it rests.  This is especially
    36	important when the proof uses a theorem, construction, or convention from
    37	Mathlib which is not part of the cited argument.  In that case the note should
    38	state the Mathlib result in ordinary mathematical language, explain how it is
    39	specialized to the notation of the paper, and compare its hypotheses and
    40	conclusion with the step it replaces.  It should not merely say that \Lean{} did
    41	not accept a proof, that the modified proof compiles, or that a named library
    42	lemma was applied.
    43	
    44	The documents in this directory should themselves follow this standard.  A
    45	policy or template which reads like a checklist will tend to produce checklist
    46	notes; the examples and templates should therefore be written as mathematical
    47	prose.
    48	
    49	\section{Concision and Readability}
    50	
    51	A paper-gap note should be short enough that a reader can understand the issue
    52	in one sitting.  The first page should answer four questions: what the source
    53	uses, how hard the remaining formal work is, what the formalization or audit
    54	checked, and what the current verdict is.  Begin with a short
    55	\emph{At a glance} section when the note concerns an open or recently resolved
    56	formalization task.  That section should estimate the difficulty, the rough
    57	implementation weight, the split between Mathlib reuse and project-local work,
    58	and the key Mathlib APIs or modules.  Use honest ranges, not false precision.
    59	
    60	The \emph{Key theorem forms} section should be Section~2, immediately after
    61	\emph{At a glance}.  Put the theorem forms before the source details so the
    62	reader knows what the formalization is aiming to prove.  After that, keep the
    63	source assertion, the mechanism being checked, the blueprint/formal comparison,
    64	and the conclusion.  Use more sections only when a counterexample or long
    65	derivation genuinely needs room.
    66	
    67	Keep background to the minimum needed for the local point.  Prefer one clear
    68	special case over a general restatement of the surrounding theorem.  Use displayed
    69	equations for the source assertion, the key calculation, and the theorem forms;
    70	avoid displays for traceability data, declaration names, or long lists.  The
    71	blueprint/formal comparison should be compact and should not repeat the theorem
    72	forms.  The section ``Form of the Note'' below specifies where traceability data
    73	belongs; the body should read as mathematical prose, not as a log.
    74	
    75	If the verdict is that there is no mathematical discrepancy, say so plainly and
    76	stop.  Keep the conclusion highly compact, normally under twenty source lines.
    77	If the only remaining work is an implementation task, name it briefly and link
    78	the issue or pull request in a footnote.
    79	
    80	\section{When the Investigation Starts}
    81	
    82	The investigation starts when the obstruction appears to be mathematical rather
    83	than merely formal.  No final judgement is needed at this stage.  It is enough
    84	that, after reading the relevant source and attempting the corresponding formal
    85	statement, the proof seems to require a different scalar, an additional
    86	hypothesis, a different tensor placement, a distinction between two objects which
    87	the prose identifies, or an auxiliary assertion not supplied by the cited
    88	argument.
    89	
    90	The same investigation should also start when such a deviation is discovered
    91	after the fact.  If the existing formal development or informal blueprint has
    92	already changed the statement, strengthened a hypothesis, weakened a conclusion,
    93	inserted an unadvertised lemma, or replaced the cited proof by a different
    94	formal-library argument, the mathematical change should be documented even if all
    95	relevant files already compile.
    96	
    97	At this early stage the purpose is to preserve the question while it is still
    98	local.  The note may later conclude that the matter is only notational, that an
    99	intermediate estimate in the cited source needs a harmless correction, that a
   100	missing hypothesis is genuinely needed, or that no discrepancy remains.  Thus
   101	the trigger is not the severity of the eventual verdict, but the appearance of a
   102	real mismatch between the cited reasoning and the statement that can be
   103	formalized.
   104	
   105	A failed tactic search, a missing formal lemma, or an inconvenient coercion is
   106	not enough.  The obstruction must survive translation back into ordinary
   107	mathematics.
   108	
   109	Sometimes an investigation uncovers an improvement that is not a discrepancy:
   110	the formalization works correctly, but it could be simplified by using an
   111	existing library, replacing a custom type, or adopting a cleaner proof route.
   112	These are not, by themselves, paper-gap notes.  They are action items.  When
   113	such an improvement is identified, open a GitHub issue or pull request that
   114	describes the proposed change.  If the investigation also produces a paper-gap
   115	note, link the issue or pull request from that note: the note records the
   116	mathematical justification, and the issue or pull request drives the
   117	implementation.
   118	
   119	\section{When to Write a Note}
   120	
   121	A note should be written once the source argument and the formal proof no longer
   122	match as mathematical arguments.  This includes, for instance, a numerical
   123	estimate whose constant does not follow from the cited lemma, a displayed
   124	conclusion which uses an unstated hypothesis, or a step in which two objects are
   125	identified although they must remain distinct.  In analytic, algebraic,
   126	probabilistic, or quantum arguments, such distinctions may concern the domain of
   127	a map, the placement of a tensor factor, the type of an outcome, the distinction
   128	between a structure and a substructure, or the scalar carried by an approximation
   129	relation.
   130	
   131	A note is required when an audit finds that a Lean declaration associated with a
   132	source-labelled statement has acquired an extra non-source hypothesis, such as
   133	bridge, residual, repair, producer, or obligation-structure data.  Such a
   134	declaration is temporary proof debt, not a replacement for the source theorem,
   135	and should not be introduced merely to avoid a \verb|sorry|.  The note must say
   136	plainly that the Lean result is conditional, identify the source-faithful theorem
   137	form that remains to be proved, and give the intended obligation discharger or
   138	removal plan.  The blueprint should not mark the source-labelled statement with
   139	\verb|\leanok| by pointing to this conditional helper.
   140	
   141	Changing a Lean theorem away from the statement in
   142	\path{references/ldt-paper/} is strongly discouraged.  A paper-gap note should
   143	not make such a change look routine: it should explain the mathematical
   144	necessity, or else classify the change as proof debt to be removed.
   145	
   146	When an existing conditional helper is audited, the first task is to extract any
   147	argument it already contains into source-faithful lemmas.  If the remaining
   148	bridge hypothesis cannot be derived from the paper hypotheses, the formal
   149	development should restore the source theorem statement and record the missing
   150	proof obligation explicitly, rather than retaining the strengthened statement as
   151	though it were the paper theorem.
   152	
   153	This requirement is not meant to classify every explicit Lean side condition as
   154	a discrepancy.  Positivity, nonemptiness, decidability, field-model instances,
   155	and denominator nonvanishing hypotheses may be faithful encodings of the domain
   156	in which the paper's theorem is stated.  The note should distinguish such
   157	boundary hypotheses from hypotheses that supply an unproved step of the paper
   158	argument.
   159	
   160	A note is also appropriate when the proof becomes formal only after changing an
   161	intermediate scalar, weakening a conclusion, strengthening a hypothesis, or
   162	inserting an additional lemma which is not simply an expansion of the cited
   163	argument.  These are mathematical changes, even when they are harmless for the
   164	final theorem.  It is likewise appropriate when an available formal-library
   165	theorem proves the needed result under a somewhat different formulation from the
   166	cited source.  In that case the note should be deliberately pedagogical.  It
   167	should explain, in ordinary mathematical language, what the replacement result
   168	says, how it is specialized, which hypotheses are new or differently packaged,
   169	and why the resulting statement is a legitimate substitute for the step in the
   170	cited argument.  If the issue remains open after reasonable attempts, the note
   171	should say what has been checked and what remains unknown.
   172	
   173	\section{Counterexamples}
   174	
   175	If the cited assertion appears to be false, the note should not stop at saying
   176	that the proof cannot be formalized.  It should give the counterexample, or the
   177	smallest relevant part of it, in ordinary mathematical notation.  The example
   178	should be accompanied by enough verification that the reader can see both sides:
   179	the hypotheses of the cited assertion hold, and its conclusion fails.
   180	
   181	When feasible, the counterexample should also be formalized in \Lean{}.  This is
   182	especially valuable when the example is finite, algebraic, computational, or
   183	otherwise small enough that the failure can be checked without reproducing the
   184	whole surrounding theory.  The note should then state the mathematical content
   185	of the checked counterexample and identify the corresponding Lean declaration in
   186	a footnote.  The Lean file is not a substitute for the prose: the prose should
   187	still explain why the example refutes the cited assertion.
   188	
   189	\section{Revision of a Note}

     2	"""Check style conventions for changed paper-gap notes.
     3	
     4	This is a local hook guard for ``docs/paper-gaps/*.tex`` notes.  The policy in
     5	``docs/paper-gaps/policy.tex`` is intentionally mathematical rather than merely
     6	syntactic, so this script does not try to certify the content of a note.  It
     7	only catches structural mistakes that reviewers should not have to catch by
     8	hand: missing front sections, missing shared macros and bibliography, and raw
     9	inline traceability which should be expressed through the paper-gap macros.
    10	
    11	The check is diff-scoped by default.  Existing archival notes are not reported
    12	unless they are changed.
    13	"""
    14	
    15	from __future__ import annotations
    16	
    17	import argparse
    18	import re
    19	import subprocess
    20	import sys
    21	from dataclasses import dataclass
    22	from pathlib import Path
    23	
    24	PAPER_GAP_PREFIX = "docs/paper-gaps/"
    25	EXCLUDED_NOTE_NAMES = {
    26	    "command.tex",
    27	    "policy.tex",
    28	    "proof-gap-protocol.tex",
    29	    "template.tex",
    30	}
    31	
    32	SECTION_RE = re.compile(r"\\section(?P<star>\*)?\{(?P<title>[^}]*)\}")
    33	CITE_RE = re.compile(r"\\cite(?:\[[^\]]*\])?\{[^}]+\}")
    34	XURL_RE = re.compile(r"\\usepackage(?:\[[^\]]*\])?\{[^}]*\bxurl\b[^}]*\}")
    35	COMMAND_INPUT_RE = re.compile(r"\\input\{(?:\./)?command\}")
    36	RAW_LEAN_ID_RE = re.compile(r"(?<!\\leanid\{)MIPStarRE\.[A-Za-z]")
    37	RAW_PAPER_PATH_RE = re.compile(r"(?<!\\path\{)references/(?:ldt|qpbt|neexp)-paper/")
    38	TEXTTT_TRACE_RE = re.compile(r"\\texttt\{(?:MIPStarRE|references/[a-z0-9-]+-paper)")
    39	
    40	
    41	@dataclass(frozen=True)
    42	class Finding:
    43	    """A structural paper-gap-note style finding."""
    44	
    45	    file: str
    46	    message: str
    47	
    48	
    49	def _is_note_file(rel_path: str) -> bool:
    50	    """Return whether ``rel_path`` is a paper-gap note governed by the guard."""
    51	
    52	    if not rel_path.startswith(PAPER_GAP_PREFIX) or not rel_path.endswith(".tex"):
    53	        return False
    54	    name = Path(rel_path).name
    55	    return name not in EXCLUDED_NOTE_NAMES
    56	
    57	
    58	def _changed_files_from_git(root: Path, *, base: str, staged: bool) -> list[str]:
    59	    """Return changed files for either the staged index or a base revision."""
    60	
    61	    command = ["git", "diff", "--name-only", "--diff-filter=ACMR"]
    62	    if staged:
    63	        command.append("--cached")
    64	    else:
    65	        command.append(base)
    66	    command.append("--")
    67	    proc = subprocess.run(
    68	        command,
    69	        cwd=root,
    70	        check=False,
    71	        stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
    72	        stderr=subprocess.PIPE,
    73	        text=True,
    74	    )
    75	    if proc.returncode != 0:
    76	        raise RuntimeError(proc.stderr.strip() or "git diff failed")
    77	    return [line.strip() for line in proc.stdout.splitlines() if line.strip()]
    78	
    79	
    80	def _read_changed_files_file(path: Path) -> list[str]:
    81	    """Read a newline-separated changed-file list."""
    82	
    83	    return [line.strip() for line in path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines() if line.strip()]
    84	
    85	
    86	def _section_titles(text: str) -> list[tuple[str, bool]]:
    87	    """Return section titles together with whether the section is starred."""
    88	
    89	    return [
    90	        (m.group("title").strip(), m.group("star") is not None)
    91	        for m in SECTION_RE.finditer(text)
    92	    ]
    93	
    94	
    95	def _first_section_body(text: str) -> str:
    96	    """Return the body of the first section, or the empty string if absent."""
    97	
    98	    matches = list(SECTION_RE.finditer(text))
    99	    if not matches:
   100	        return ""
   101	    start = matches[0].end()
   102	    end = matches[1].start() if len(matches) > 1 else len(text)
   103	    return text[start:end]
   104	
   105	
   106	def _scan_note_text(rel_path: str, text: str) -> list[Finding]:
   107	    """Return style findings for one paper-gap note."""
   108	
   109	    findings: list[Finding] = []
   110	
   111	    def add(message: str) -> None:
   112	        findings.append(Finding(rel_path, message))
   113	
   114	    if "\\documentclass" not in text:
   115	        add("missing LaTeX document class")
   116	    if not XURL_RE.search(text):
   117	        add("missing `\\usepackage{xurl}`")
   118	    if not COMMAND_INPUT_RE.search(text):
   119	        add("missing shared paper-gap macros: `\\input{command}`")
   120	    if "\\begin{document}" not in text or "\\end{document}" not in text:
   121	        add("missing document body delimiters")
   122	
   123	    sections = _section_titles(text)
   124	    if len(sections) < 2:
   125	        add("missing first two sections `At a glance` and `Key theorem forms`")
   126	    else:
   127	        first_title, first_starred = sections[0]
   128	        second_title, second_starred = sections[1]
   129	        if first_starred or first_title != "At a glance":
   130	            add("Section 1 must be an unstarred `At a glance` section")
   131	        if second_starred or not second_title.startswith("Key theorem forms"):
   132	            add("Section 2 must be an unstarred `Key theorem forms` section")
   133	
   134	    first_body = _first_section_body(text).lower()
   135	    if first_body:
   136	        if "difficulty" not in first_body:
   137	            add("the `At a glance` section should state the difficulty")
   138	        if "estimated weight" not in first_body:
   139	            add("the `At a glance` section should state the estimated weight")
   140	        if "mathlib/project split" not in first_body:
   141	            add("the `At a glance` section should state the Mathlib/project split")
   142	        has_key_inputs = (
   143	            "key mathlib inputs" in first_body
   144	            or "key mathematical inputs" in first_body
   145	        )
   146	        if not has_key_inputs:
   147	            add(
   148	                "the `At a glance` section should state the key Mathlib or "
   149	                "mathematical inputs"
   150	            )
   151	
   152	    if "\\section{Conclusion}" not in text:
   153	        add("missing `Conclusion` section")
   154	    if "\\bibliographystyle{alpha}" not in text:
   155	        add("missing `\\bibliographystyle{alpha}`")
   156	    if "\\bibliography{references}" not in text:
   157	        add("missing `\\bibliography{references}`")
   158	    if not CITE_RE.search(text):
   159	        add("missing bibliographic citation such as `\\cite{...}`")
   160	    if ("\\ghissue{" not in text and "\\ghpr{" not in text
   161	            and "\\localissue{" not in text):
   162	        add("missing traceability macro `\\ghissue{...}`, `\\ghpr{...}`, "
   163	            "or `\\localissue{...}`")
   164	
   165	    if TEXTTT_TRACE_RE.search(text):
   166	        add("use paper-gap macros instead of `\\texttt{...}` for Lean or source traceability")
   167	    if RAW_LEAN_ID_RE.search(text):
   168	        add("wrap fully qualified Lean names with `\\leanid{...}`")
   169	    if RAW_PAPER_PATH_RE.search(text):
   170	        add("wrap paper source paths with `\\path{...}`")
   171	
   172	    return findings
   173	
   174	
   175	def scan_changed_notes(root: Path, changed_files: list[str]) -> list[Finding]:
   176	    """Return findings for changed paper-gap notes."""
   177	
   178	    findings: list[Finding] = []
   179	    for rel_path in sorted({path for path in changed_files if _is_note_file(path)}):
   180	        path = root / rel_path
   181	        if not path.exists():
   182	            continue
   183	        text = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
   184	        findings.extend(_scan_note_text(rel_path, text))
   185	    return findings
   186	
   187	
   188	def _parse_args(argv: list[str]) -> argparse.Namespace:
   189	    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
   190	    parser.add_argument("--root", type=Path, default=Path("."))
   191	    parser.add_argument("--base", default="origin/main")
   192	    parser.add_argument("--staged", action="store_true")
   193	    parser.add_argument("--changed-files", nargs="*")
   194	    parser.add_argument("--changed-files-file", type=Path)
   195	    parser.add_argument("--ci", action="store_true")
   196	    return parser.parse_args(argv)
   197	
   198	
   199	def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
   200	    args = _parse_args(sys.argv[1:] if argv is None else argv)
   201	    root = args.root.resolve()
   202	
   203	    try:
   204	        if args.changed_files_file is not None:
   205	            changed_files = _read_changed_files_file(args.changed_files_file)
   206	        elif args.changed_files is not None:
   207	            changed_files = list(args.changed_files)
   208	        else:
   209	            changed_files = _changed_files_from_git(root, base=args.base, staged=args.staged)
   210	    except RuntimeError as exc:
   211	        print(f"check_paper_gap_note_style.py: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
   212	        return 2
   213	
   214	    findings = scan_changed_notes(root, changed_files)
   215	    if findings:
   216	        print("Paper-gap note style findings:", file=sys.stderr)
   217	        for finding in findings:
   218	            print(f"  {finding.file}: {finding.message}", file=sys.stderr)
   219	        return 1 if args.ci else 0
   220	
   221	    if args.ci:

   223	        print(f"Paper-gap note style check passed for {checked} changed note(s).")
